en: With their insights and the movement of their hands, men have generated from the two fire-sticks Agni, the praiseworthy one,
visible from afar, the lord of the house, the radiant one.
The Vasus established that Agni in his dwelling, him who is beautiful to behold for protection from every side—
he who is worthy of skill, who is constant within the house.
O Agni, most youthful one, shine brightly before us, kindled with an unfailing flame;
unto you all sacrificial strengths ever approach.
May these fires of yours shine forth more excellently than other fires, bestowing heroic sons, radiant and glorious,
where well-born men sit together in assembly.
O Agni, O powerful one, grant us through our prayer wealth consisting of brave sons and good progeny,
which is praiseworthy and which no sorcerer can overcome by his magic power.
To him, the very skillful one, the young woman approaches with the oblation at evening and at dawn—the ladle dripping with ghee;
to him, Aramati, seeking wealth, approaches of her own accord.
O Agni, burn away all hostile powers with those heats by which you consumed Jarūtha;
drive far away the disease that causes groaning.
O Agni, you whose face they kindle, O most excellent, bright, radiant, and purifying one—
through these our praises, may you be present here with us.
O Agni, those mortal men of our fathers who have in many places shared in your countenance—
through them, may you be well-disposed toward us here.
May these men, heroes in the slaying of Vṛtra, overcome all godless illusions—
those who have admired my well-praised prayer.
O Agni, let us not sit in the void among men, nor around you in want of food or lack of heroes; O dweller in the house, dwell in houses filled with progeny.
To that sacrifice which the horse-attendant constantly approaches, grant us a dwelling rich in progeny and noble offspring,
increasing through its own birth and its abundance.
Protect us, O Agni, from the unpleasant Rakṣas; protect us from the malice of the stingy man who offers no gifts.
With you as my ally, may I overcome those who attack us in battle.
May this Agni surpass all other fires, where the vigorous son with strong hands and a thousand paths meets with the imperishable syllable.
May that Agni protect the kindler from the one who seeks to harm him; may he deliver him from distress. Well-born heroes move about him in attendance.
This is that Agni, invoked in many places, whom the Lord, possessing oblations, kindles with fuel;
him the Hotṛ-priest goes around at the sacrifices.
O Agni, may we, being masters, offer unto thee many perpetual oblations;
performing both modes of conveyance at the sacrificial feast.
O Agni, bear these most welcome oblations toward the assembly of the gods;
may they accept our fragrant offerings.
O Agni, do not deliver us over to one who is childless, nor to ill-will, nor to this lack of wisdom;
O observer of Truth, do not abandon us to hunger, nor to the demon, neither in our home nor in the forest.
Now, O Agni, instruct my prayers; O God, grant them favor for the sake of the patrons.
May we both partake in your gift. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Agni, you who are easy to invoke and beautiful to behold, shine forth with your brilliant light, O Son of Strength!
Let no one among our own kin, nor any manly hero, ever fail us while we are together with you and our offspring.
O Agni, do not proclaim us to those who hold us in contempt while these fires, kindled by the gods, burn; let not your ill-will, O Son of Strength, reach us even through your impetuousness.
O Agni, that mortal man of noble countenance who, being wealthy, offers oblations to you, the immortal— he, as a patron,
establishes the gods as the winners of riches for him whom he, seeking his goal, approaches with inquiry.
O Agni, you who know of great prosperity, bring to our patrons vast wealth,
so that we, O powerful one, may rejoice with undiminished life and heroic sons.
Now, O Agni, instruct my prayers; you, O God, make them successful for our patrons. May we both be participants in your bounty. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Agni, enjoy our fuel today; blaze forth mightily, sending up your worshipful smoke. Touch the celestial ridge with your flames; extend yourself with your rays across the beams of the sun.
We shall praise with sacrifices the greatness of Narāśaṃsa, the worshipful one, of these [gods],
who are wise, pure, and bestowers of inspired thought— the gods who relish both kinds of oblations.

We shall ever exalt for our sacrifice Agni, who is worthy of praise, the Asura, the highly skillful, the messenger between the two worlds (Heaven and Earth) whose speech is true— the one kindled by Manu, like Manu himself.
Worshipping and bringing [offerings] on their knees, they spread the sacrificial grass with reverence before Agni.
O Adhvaryus, pouring [libations], cleanse with the oblation the one whose back is sprinkled with ghee, the speckled one.
The pious ones, seeking the gods, have thrown open the doors at the assembly of the deities, longing for the chariot.
Like two mothers licking their young, they have adorned themselves like virgins at festivals.
And may the two divine maidens, Dawn and Night, like a cow easy to milk,
sit upon our sacred grass— O much-invoked, wealthy, and worshipful ones, may they both take their place for our well-being.
O inspired poets, singers at the human sacrifices, I deem you two to be the Jātavedases whom I must worship.
Having raised up our sacrifice during our invocations, may you two win desirable boons among the gods.
May Bhāratī, in harmony with the Bhāratīs, and Iḷā with the gods, and Agni with men,
and Sarasvatī with the Sarasvatas— may these three goddesses come hither and sit upon this sacred grass.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, bestowing it upon us, release that generative seed which nourishes;
from which is born a hero, skillful in action, highly dexterous, one who sets the pressing-stones in motion, and a lover of the gods.
O Lord of the Forest, release [the oblation] toward the gods; let Agni, the immolator, prepare the offering.
He, indeed, as the most truthful Hotar-priest, shall sacrifice, for he knows the generations of the gods.
Come hither, O Agni, being well-kindled, on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods.
Let Aditi, the mother of noble sons, sit upon our sacrificial grass; let the immortal gods rejoice in the Svāhā-call!
In unison with the fires, make Agni your god— the most excellent sacrificer, the messenger at the rite—
him who is firmly established among mortals, the upholder of *ṛta*, whose head is flame, whose food is ghee, the purifier.
Like a neighing horse eager for pasture, when he has stepped forth from the great enclosure, then the wind blows after his flame; and so, thy path becomes black.
O Agni, whose flames, once kindled, ageless and newly born, rise up from you, the bull;
the ruddy smoke goes toward heaven, for as the messenger, O Agni, you hasten to the gods.

O you whose power spread across the earth when you swiftly seized your food with your jaws; like an unleashed army, your net advances; O wondrous one, you pluck it out with your tongue as if it were barley.
Men groom him at evening and at dawn—him, the youngest Agni—like a steed;
sharpening him in his own dwelling as a guest, the flame of the bull who has been offered oblations shines forth.
O you of beautiful countenance, your face is lovely to behold when it shines near us like gold;
your roar goes forth like the thunder of heaven, and you display your splendor like the wondrous sun.
So that we may offer to you with the cry of *svāhā* to Agni, with oblations accompanied by praises and rich in clarified butter—
O Agni, protect us with those immeasurable glories of yours, within a hundred fortresses of iron.
O Jātavedas, Son of Strength, with those invincible hymns which you have for the donor, or those by which you protect the manly ones— protect us with them, along with our patrons and singers.
When he goes forth, pure like a sharpened axe, shining with his own form and beauty;
he who was born from his two parents as one desirable for the sacrifice to the gods, the wise and purifying one.

O Agni, shine forth these blessings upon us; may we attain a well-disposed will. May all things be favorable for the singers and the one who praises you. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Bring forth an offering and a well-purified hymn for your Agni, for his bright luster—
He who, by means of his wisdom, moves between all divine and human generations.
May that Agni be skillful even though he is young, he from whom, as the youngest, he was born of his mother;
he who, bright-toothed, embraces the forests and instantly devours even abundant food.

In the assembly and before the face of this god, whom mortals have seized as the bright one— Agni, who has uttered a cry of defiance against the human capture, has shone forth for the Āyu, difficult to overcome.

This seer among those who are not seers, this wise Agni, the immortal, has been established among mortals. O powerful one, do not lead us astray in this matter; may we always be well-disposed toward you.
He who has occupied the god-fashioned womb— for by his will Agni has transcended the immortals—
him the plants and the trees, and the earth, bear as their embryo, he who nourishes all.
For Agni is the lord of abundant immortality; he is the lord of wealth and the giver of heroic strength.
O powerful one, may we not sit around you without sons, without cattle, or without food.
For the wealth of the stranger is to be shared; may we be masters of our own eternal riches.
O Agni, there is no offspring of another that remains as a remnant for us; do not lead us astray from the path of the mindless.
For a stranger, however well-disposed, is not to be grasped as one’s own kin in thought;
yet he returns again to his home. May the prize-winning steed, our new protector, come toward us.
O Agni, protect us from the one who seeks to harm us; O powerful one, guard us from reproach.
Let the smoke-enveloped path reach you, and may desirable, thousandfold wealth come to us.

O Agni, shine forth these blessings upon us; may we attain a wise and noble resolve. May all things be well for those who praise you and sing your hymns. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Bring forth a song of praise to the mighty Agni, the messenger of heaven and earth;
he who, as Vaiśvānara, has grown strong in the lap of all the immortals through those who keep watch.
Agni has been established in heaven and on earth; he is the leader of the rivers, the bull of standing waters.
Vaiśvānara, growing strong by his choice, shines forth upon the human tribes.
Out of fear of you, the dark tribes fled in different directions, abandoning their possessions, O Vaiśvānara,
when you shone forth for Pūru, blazing and bursting open their fortresses, O Agni.
O Vaiśvānara Agni, both the earth and the sky abide within your threefold ordinance;
blazing with undecaying luster, you have overspread the two worlds with your light.
O Agni, the bay horses, lowing toward you, and the resonant songs dripping with ghee attend upon you—
the Lord of the peoples, the charioteer of riches, Vaiśvānara, the banner of the dawns and of days.
In you the Vasus established their divine power, for they took pleasure in your will, O you who are great like Mitra;
O Agni, you drove the Dasyus from their home, generating broad light for the Ārya.
Being born in the highest heaven, like Vāyu you instantly protect the path;
generating the worlds, O Jātavedas, you cried out, bestowing gifts for the sake of offspring.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, Jātavedas, send forth to us that glorious nourishment,
by which you, O possessor of all boons, swell our wealth and bestow wide renown upon the mortal who offers oblations.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, bestow upon our liberal patrons that wealth which provides abundant food and is renowned as strength;
grant us great protection, O Agni, being in harmony with the Rudras and the Vasus.
I celebrate the glorious deeds of the sovereign Asura, the man who is to be exulted by the peoples; like those of Indra, the mighty, I praise his exploits, and praising him, I speak forth my song.
They urge forth the sage, the banner, the nourishment, the light from the mountain—the auspicious sovereignty over heaven and earth.
With songs, I celebrate the ancient, great deeds of Agni, the breaker of forts.

Agni has driven away those Dasyus—the unrighteous, the knotted, the speakers of insults, the Paṇis, the faithless, the non-prosperous, and the non-sacrificers. He, the first, has made those who do not sacrifice their successors.
He, the most heroic, who by his powers turned toward the east those [waters] sporting in the western darkness—
him, Agni, the lord of wealth, the unbending subduer of those who attack us, I praise.
He who made the dwelling-places free from disease with his deadly weapons, and who made the Dawns have noble lords as their husbands—
he, the mighty Agni, having subdued the Nahuṣas, by his powers made the clans bringers of tribute.
In whose protection all people have taken their stand, seeking his favor—
Agni Vaiśvānara has sat down in the chosen lap of the two worlds, the parents.
The god Vaiśvānara has taken up the treasures from the depths at the rising of the sun;
from the lower ocean and from the further one, Agni has taken them up from heaven and from earth.
I impel with salutations the god Agni, the powerful one, like a prize-winning steed;
may he, the wise one, become our messenger for the sacrifice, for he has himself found his place among the gods as one who moves with measured pace.
Come, O Agni, along your own paths, you who are delightful, enjoying the friendship of the gods;
making the ridges of the earth roar with your vital strengths, burn down all the forests at your will with your jaws.
The sacrifice is directed eastward, for the sacred grass is well-placed; Agni, being invoked like a Hotṛ priest, is gratified.
Calling upon the two Mothers who possess all boons, from whom you were born, O youngest one, you have become most gracious.
At once, at the sacrifice, the wise men brought forth the charioteer who belongs to them;
Agni, the lord of the people, has been established in the dwelling as the joyful, sweet-voiced, and truth-abiding guardian of the house.
The chosen bearer has sat down, having arrived; Agni is the priest in the assembly of men, the distributor.
He whom both Heaven and Earth have magnified—he, the all-desirable one, the Hotṛ-priest worships.
These men have surpassed everything with their splendors—those heroes who have fashioned the prayer as a choice treasure;
they who, listening, furthered the people, and who have meditated upon this my *ṛta*.
Now we Vasiṣṭhas implore you, O Agni, the lord of riches, O Son of Strength; grant nourishment to our singers and to our patrons. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
The noble King is kindled with prostrations, he whose face is anointed with clarified butter;
men, pressing forward with oblations, worship him; Agni has shone forth at the head of the dawns.
And this very one has been recognized as the great, delightful Hotṛ of men, the youthful Agni;
having spread himself over the earth, he has shone forth, and with blackened furrows he has grown great among the plants.
By what hymn, O Agni, will you favor us? What power will you exercise when you are praised?
When, O bounteous giver, shall we become masters of wealth, winners of riches that are invincible and excellent?
This Agni of Bharata is heard of further and further, as he shines forth with great light like the sun;
he who has stood firm against the Pūrus in battles, the shining divine guest, has blazed up.
Abundant oblations have been placed within you; be well-disposed toward us with all your flames.
O Agni, though already praised and being lauded, you are heard; O well-born one, increase your own body by yourself.
May this speech, winning hundreds and thousands, arise for Agni with double strength—
so that it may be a blessing to the singers and to the patron, brilliant, driving away disease, and slaying the Rākṣasas.
Now we Vasiṣṭhas entreat you, O Agni, the lord of riches, O Son of Strength;
bring nourishment to our singers and our patrons. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
The lover of the dawns has awakened from their lap—the delightful Hotṛ, the most wise, the purifier.
He establishes the banner for both classes of beings; he places offerings among the gods and wealth among the doers of good deeds.
He is the one of skillful wisdom who forced open the doors of the Paṇis, purifying for us the hymn that provides much nourishment.
The joyous Hotṛ-priest, the domestic lord of the people, has become visible through the darkness of the nights.
Unerring sage, Aditi, Vivasvat, Mitra who speaks kindly—may he be auspicious to us as our guest.
With brilliant luster, he shines at the forefront of the dawns; the embryo of the waters has entered the plants.
Worthy of invocation by men through the ages, Jātavedas has shone forth, gathering together from all sides;
he who shines with a beautiful appearance and radiant light, the cows have awakened as he is kindled.
O Agni, go on your mission as messenger; do not fail, but proceed toward the gods with the company of those who compose sacred hymns.
Sacrifice to Sarasvatī, to the Maruts, to the Aśvins, and to the Waters—offer sacrifice to all the gods for the bestowing of treasures.
O Agni, Vasiṣṭha, kindling you, has slain Jarūtha; sacrifice for wealth and for abundance.
O Jātavedas, sing your many songs of praise; and may you all protect us evermore with blessings.
Like the lover of the Dawn, he has spread his broad expanse, flashing, shining, and glowing;
the bright, golden bull shines with light, and inciting our yearning prayers, he has awakened them.
Like the sun at dawn, Agni has shone forth at the break of day; like the *uśij* performing a sacrifice, he has extended his thought.
Agni, the god who knows all births, hastens as the messenger who goes to the gods, the most effective seeker of gain.
Toward Agni proceed our songs and thoughts, seeking the gods and begging for wealth—
toward him who is beautiful to behold, of fair countenance, swift-moving, the bearer of oblations, the messenger of mankind.
O Agni, being in harmony with the Vasus, bring Indra to us; bring the great Rudra with the Rudras;
bring Aditi, who is kind to all people, with the Ādityas; and Bṛhaspati, the possessor of all boons, with the chanters of hymns.
The eager people invoke at the sacrifices Agni, the most youthful Hotṛ, the melodious one;
for he has become the protector of riches, the unwearied messenger for the worship of the gods.
Great is your heralding of this sacrifice; the immortals do not rejoice without you.
Come hither on one chariot with all the gods; O Agni, sit down here as the first Hotṛ-priest.
Men with oblations ever invoke you, the swift one, for the office of messenger;
he upon whose sacred grass you sit with the gods, O Agni—for him the days become auspicious.
Even from three nights past, the treasures have been made manifest within you for the mortal who offers oblations.
Like Manu, O Agni, worship the gods here; be our messenger and our protector against curses.
Agni is the lord of the great sacrifice; Agni [is the lord] of every oblation that has been prepared.
For the Vasus delight in his ritual wisdom, and thus the gods have established him as the bearer of the oblations.
O Agni, bring the gods here to consume the oblation; let them, with Indra as their chief, rejoice here.
Place this sacrifice among the gods in heaven. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
We have approached with great homage the youngest [Agni], who has shone forth, well-kindled in his own dwelling—
the one of wondrous luster between the two wide worlds, well-invoked, facing every direction.
He, Agni Jātavedas, who by his greatness overcomes all difficulties, is praised in our home;
may he protect us from misfortune and from reproach—both us who sing his praises and our patrons.
O Agni, you are Varuṇa and you are Mitra; the Vasiṣṭhas magnify you with their hymns.
May all treasures easy to win be found in you. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
Bring forth a prayer and a hymn for Agni, the all-illuminating, the supporter of devotion, the slayer of the Asuras— like one who, being pleased,
offers an oblation upon the sacred grass— to Vaiśvānara, the director of our thoughts.
O Agni, flaming with your brilliance at birth, you filled the two worlds, heaven and earth;
O Vaiśvānara Jātavedas, by your greatness, you released the gods from the curse.
When you were born, O Agni, you looked out upon all beings like a watchful herdsman wandering around his cattle.
O Vaiśvānara, find a path for our sacred prayer; and do you all protect us always with your blessings.
With fuel, with invocations of the gods,
and with oblations, may we, full of reverence, worship Agni Jātavedas, the god of bright luster.
O Agni, may we honor you with fuel; may we worship you, O worthy of sacrifice, with beautiful hymns.
O Hotṛ of the rite, may we worship you with clarified butter; O God of auspicious luster, may we worship you with the oblation.
O Agni, come with the gods to our invocation of the gods, taking pleasure in our *vaṣaṭ*-utterance.
May we be those who offer gifts to you, the god; and may you all protect us always with blessings.
Offer the oblation into the mouth of the bounteous one who is to be approached,
he who is our nearest kinsman.
He who has sat down over the five tribes in every house— the sage, the young master of the household.
May Agni protect our household wealth on every side;
and may he deliver us from distress.
I have generated a new hymn for Agni, the falcon of heaven; will he not surely grant us wealth?
Whose desirable splendors are for all to see, like the wealth of a hero,
as he blazes at the forefront of the sacrifice.
May Agni accept this *vaṣaṭ*-utterance; may he graciously enjoy our songs of praise—he, the best of sacrificers, the bearer of oblations.
O Lord of the People, O God, we establish you, the radiant one, rich in heroes, within our reach, O Agni, you who are invoked with oblations.
Shine through the nights and the dawns; with you as our good fire, may we be well-provided with heroes, for you are well-disposed toward us.
The inspired singers approach you for gain with their prayers;
the thousandfold speech approaches you.
Agni, the immortal with bright radiance, drives away the demons; he is pure, purifying, and worthy of praise.
As the lord of power, O young son of strength, bring us riches;
and may Bhaga grant us what is desirable.
O Agni, you [grant] glory accompanied by heroic sons; and Savitṛ the god, Bhaga, and Diti bestow desirable wealth.
O Agni, protect us from distress; O God, burn against those who seek to harm us with your most scorching, ageless flames.
And so, for our protection, be a great, unassailable iron fortress for the defense of men,
a citadel with a hundredfold strength.
Protect us from distress, O illuminator of the night, from the one who intends evil; protect us by day and by night, O invincible one.
With this homage, I invoke for you Agni, the Son of Strength— the beloved,
most wise steward of the sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all.
He yokes his two ruddy steeds that provide all sustenance; well-invoked, let him hasten hither.
May this sacrifice, accompanied by excellent prayers and performed with skillful labor, bring the divine bounty of the Vasus to the people.
The flame of this bounteous one has risen up as he is being invoked;
the ruddy smoke-clouds, touching the heavens, the men kindle together.
We make you our most glorious messenger; bring the gods here for the feast.
O Son of Strength, bestow all the enjoyments of mortals that we entreat of you.
O Agni, you are the master of the house; you are our Hotṛ at the sacrifice.
You are the Potṛ, O possessor of all boons, the wise one; perform the sacrifice and go toward what is desirable.
Bestow wealth upon the sacrificer, O you of noble wisdom, for you are indeed the bestower of riches.
Sharpen us at the rite, every priest who is well-praised and skillful.
O Agni, well-invoked with *svāhā*, may the wise patrons be dear to you—
those generous lords of men who bestow wide pastures of cattle.
Those in whose home Iḷā, with butter in her hand, sits down as she is invited—protect them from malice and reproach, O Victorious One; grant us shelter that is far-renowned.
With his pleasant tongue and mouth, the most wise bearer [of the sacrifice],
O Agni, bring wealth to us and to our patrons, and perfect the offering of the oblation.
Those who bestow gifts of horses and great wealth out of a desire for high renown—
O youngest one, protect them from distress with your hundred fortresses as their deliverers.
The god Draviṇodas desires from you a full ladle poured out;
either pour it up or fill it up, for then the god will take heed of you.
The gods have made him the Hotṛ of the sacrifice, the wise one, the bearer;
Agni bestows treasure and heroic strength upon the person who worships and gives.
O Agni, be well-kindled with excellent fuel, and let the sacrificial grass be spread out widely.
And let the longing doors swing wide open; and bring hither the longing gods.
O Agni, come with the oblation and worship the gods; O Jātavedas, make the sacrifice well-performed.
May Jātavedas perform the sacrifice well; may he worship the immortal gods and satisfy them.
Win for us all desirable things, O wise one; may our prayers be fulfilled this day.
The gods, O Agni, have established you as the bearer of oblations, the Son of Strength.
May we be those who offer worship to you, O God; approaching you, may you distribute great treasures to us.

For indeed, O Indra, all desirable things which our fathers, the singers, won from you—you possess the well-milking cows and the horses; you are the one who most effectively wins wealth for the seeker of the gods.
For like a king among his wives, you shall dwell here; as a wise seer, protect us through the days.
O Maghavan, sharpen our songs with cattle and horses; favor us for the sake of wealth.
These delightful songs, vying with one another here and seeking the gods, have approached you.
May your path of wealth come hither; may we abide in your favor and protection, O Indra.
Like one desiring to milk a cow in a field rich with grass, Vasiṣṭha has poured forth his prayers to you. All people call you my lord of cattle; may Indra come toward us with his favor.
Even the spreading floods, O Indra, you made shallow and easy to cross for Sudās;
you, the newest singer of hymns, turned the arrogant Śimyu’s curses and the rivers’ malevolence against him.
Puroḷā and Turvaśa were eager for sacrifice; like fish driven by hunger, they were intent upon wealth.
The Bhṛgus and Druhyus showed obedience; as a friend, he helped his friend across the two opposing sides.
The Pakthas, Bhalānasas, Alinas, Viṣāṇins, and Śivas have come;
he who led the Arya’s companions has come through battle to the Tṛtsus for the sake of cattle and men.
Those of evil intent, seeking to cause Aditi to flow away, mindless, have seized the Paruṣṇī.
Ruling over the earth with his greatness, the seer lay watching over the cattle.
They went for gain, not for loss; even the swift one did not reach the Paruṣṇī.
Indra subdued Sudās’s well-impelled enemies, those of servile speech among men.
They have gone forth like cattle from the pasture without a herdsman, gathering toward their appointed friend;
with spotted kine, urged on by the spotted one, the teams and the chariots have rendered obedience.
The king who, out of desire for glory, cast down one and twenty people of the two Vaikarṇas;
like a wondrous worker at his station, he trimmed the sacrificial grass, and the hero Indra made their release.
Then the thunderbolt-armed [Indra] cast down the famous, aged Kavaṣa into the waters along with the Druhyu.
Here, those who sought your friendship and rejoiced in following you chose you for their alliance.
Indra, by his might, instantly shattered all their firm fortresses—seven in number.
He won back the household of the Ānava for the Tṛtsu; may we conquer Pūru, the speaker of insults, in the assembly.
Desiring cattle, the Anavas and Druhyus—sixty hundred, six thousand, and sixty-six heroes—have fallen asleep; all these heroic deeds were performed by Indra.
Under Indra’s guidance, these Tr̥tsus, exerting themselves, rushed downward like released waters;
the ill-disposed ones, measuring out their own destruction, abandoned all their provisions to Sudās.

The half of the hero who drinks the cooked offering but lacks Indra—him, the arrogant one, Indra has driven far away to the earth. Indra has measured out the fury against the furious; he has taken his place upon the paths as the master of the track.
Even with the weak he performed that one great deed; even the lioness he struck down with a ram.
Indra cut away the corners of the dwelling for the householder; he bestowed all provisions upon Sudās.
For all your enemies have indeed submitted to you; find the weak point even of the defiant Bheda.
O Indra, hurl your sharp thunderbolt down upon him who harms those mortals who praise you.
The Yamunā and the Tr̥tsus aided Indra; here he plundered Bheda and stripped him of all his possessions.
The Ajas, the Śigrus, and the Yakṣvas brought him tribute—their heads, including those of horses.
O Indra, your favors and your riches cannot be fully surveyed, whether ancient or new, like the dawns.
You struck down even Devaka who considered himself important; you yourself shattered the mighty Śambara.
Those who, out of devotion to you, have rejoiced from their homes—Parāśara, Śatayātu, and Vasiṣṭha—let them not forget the friendship of you, the Bhoja; then may fair days dawn for our patrons.
Two hundred cows from the grandson of Devavat, two chariots with brides from Sudās—
worthy of this gift from Paijavana, O Agni, I go around like a Hotṛ priest at the sacrificial seat, chanting my praise.
The four gifts of Paijavana, accompanied by well-disposed attendants and adorned with pearls, have come to me in abundance;
the bay steeds of Sudās, standing upon the earth, carry my offspring for the sake of progeny and glory.

He whose fame lies between the two wide worlds, who has distributed [wealth] head by head as a distributor—him, Indra, the seven rivers praise; he has sharpened his weapon for the combat in the encounter.
O Maruts, heroes, attend upon this Divodāsa as a father attends upon Sudās;
protect the intention of Paijavana, his difficult-to-attain, undecaying, and much-desired dominion.
He who, like a fearsome bull with sharpened horns, alone causes all the peoples to tremble;
he who is the one from whom you take away the wealth of every non-offering man, and bestow it upon the one who presses the soma.
O Indra, you indeed protected Kutsa in that battle, listening with your own body;
for you, desiring to help the son of Arjuni, subjected the Dāsa Śuṣṇa and Kuyava to him.
O bold one, with your boldness you have protected Sudās, whose oblations were accepted, with all your aids;
you protected Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, and Pūru at the winning of land and in the slayings of Vṛtra.
O you whose mind is directed toward men, O Lord of the bay horses, you slay many Vṛtras at the banquet of the gods with your heroic followers;
you sent the Dasyus Cumuri and Dhuni to sleep for the sake of Dabhīti, making them easy to overcome.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, those were your mighty exploits when you instantly struck down ninety-nine forts;
you cast the hundredth into its dwelling, and you slew Vṛtra and Namuci as well.
Ancient indeed are those enjoyments of yours, O Indra, granted to Sudās, the donor who offers oblations.
For you, the bull, I yoke the two vigorous bay steeds; may our prayers reach you, O most powerful one, and win the prize.

O powerful Lord of the bay horses, let us not fall into misfortune through this your siege; do not abandon us to the wicked. Protect us with your safe defenses, and may we remain dear to you among the patrons.
O Maghavan, may we men, as dear friends, rejoice under your protection and in your favor.
Subdue Turvaśa and Yadu; you who intend to perform a praiseworthy deed for Atithigva, sharpen your weapons against them.
O Maghavan, at once indeed in your favor, men who recite hymns proclaim their songs of praise;
you who, through our invocations, have scattered the Panis—choose us for that very alliance.
O most heroic man, may these hymns of men, directed toward us and bestowing riches, be for you;
O Indra, be auspicious to them in the slaying of Vṛtra—be the friend, the hero, and the protector of those men.
Now, O heroic Indra, being praised for your aid, strengthened by our prayer, increase yourself in body; bestow upon us wealth and followers. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
The fierce one, self-dependent, was born for heroic valor; the manly one made the waters flow as he was about to act.
The youth went to the assembly of men with his aids; O Indra, you are our protector even from great sin.
Indra, waxing mighty, shall slay Vṛtra; now the Hero has helped his singer with his aid.
He has indeed created wide space for Sudās, and he has repeatedly become the giver of wealth to the donor.

Fighting, irresistible, stirring up conflict, a conqueror in battle, a hero, ever-victorious, and unconquered from birth— Indra, possessing innate strength, has scattered the hostile armies and then struck down every foe who acted as an enemy.
O Indra, mighty one, you have filled both worlds with your greatness and your powers.
Indra, the lord of bay horses, brandishing his thunderbolt, has proclaimed himself through the exhilaration of the soma-juice in the midst of the intoxications.
The bull has procreated the bull for the sake of battle; even the woman has brought forth that manly one.
He who stands as a leader of armies for men is the uninjured hero, the seeker of cattle, the bold one.
Never indeed does that person falter, nor shall he suffer harm, who seeks to win over his formidable mind;
he who offers worship with sacrifices and pays homage to Indra, being a guardian of Truth and born of Truth, shall rule over wealth.
O Indra, when you, the elder, bestowing aid upon the younger, gave a gift more excellent than that of the lesser;
O Wondrous One, as one who dwells in immortality, bring us far-reaching and marvelous wealth.
O Indra, wielder of the stone, that dear person who offers gifts to you shall be your exclusive friend.
May we be most highly favored by this benevolence of yours, and may we abide in the protection and the heroic guardianship of you, the unslayable one.
This hymn has cried out to you as a bull; it has reached its goal, O Maghavan, and has implored you.
The desire for wealth has come upon your singer; therefore, O Śakra, do you indeed help us toward riches.
O Indra, grant that food to us through our devotion to you, and to those liberal patrons who themselves incite us;
may your excellent power be truly for the singer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
The divine, cattle-strengthening juice has been pressed; Indra has taken pleasure in it from his very birth.
We awaken you with sacrifices, O Lord of the bay horses; take notice of our hymn during the exhilaration of the soma-juice.
They go forth to the sacrifice, they spread the sacred grass; drinking Soma at the assembly, they are loud-voiced.
They are brought down from the grasp of glory—those far-resounding bulls who seek out men.
O Indra, you made the many waters flow, which had been obstructed by the serpent, O hero;
at your roar they turned back like chariot-horses, and all artificial things tremble in fear.
The terrible Indra, knowing all manly deeds, seized them with his weapons; exulting, he shattered their fortresses, and with his thunderbolt in hand, he struck them down by his might.
Neither sorcerers, O Indra, nor those who praise us with their knowledge have incited us, O Most Mighty One.
May he prevail over the hostile and perverse creature; let not the phallus-worshippers obstruct our sacred law.
O Indra, you have surpassed all by your wisdom upon the earth; the realms of space cannot encompass your greatness.
For with your own power you struck down Vṛtra; no enemy could find the end of you in battle.
Even the ancient gods measured out their powers for your sake, for your divine sovereignty and dominion.
Indra, having overcome all, distributes riches; they invoke Indra for the winning of booty.
For even the humble singer has invoked you for protection, O Indra, lord of abundant fortune.
You have been our helper, O you of a hundred aids; you are the defender of one such as I who bestows gifts.

O Indra, may we be your friends forever, increasing our reverence through your greatness, O Deliverer! May they surely overcome the enemy's assault in battle by your protection, and may they subdue the strength of those who seek to conquer us.
O Indra, grant him food through your devotion—both him and those liberal patrons who themselves incite us;
let there be excellent power for your singer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Drink the Soma, O Indra; let that which the stone has pressed for you exhilarate you, well-guided by the arms of the presser like a courser.
That exhilarating draught of yours which is worthy of union and beautiful, by which you slay the Vṛtras, O Lord of the Bay Steeds—
let that intoxicate you, O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth.
O Maghavan, take heed of this my speech, this hymn of praise which Vasiṣṭha recites for you;
enjoy these sacred prayers at our shared feast.
Hear the call of the pressing-stone as it drinks; take notice of the inspired thought of the sage who chants. Accept these most intimate acts of devotion; may we be united with them.
I do not forget your songs, nor the well-spoken praise of you, the swift Asura; knowing them, I ever proclaim your name, O self-glorious one.
For many indeed are your libations among men; the wise man invokes you alone.
O Maghavan, do not keep us away from our enemies for long.
For you alone, O Hero, are all these libations; for you I fashion these strengthening prayers.
You are to be invoked by men at all times.
Never indeed, O fierce Dasyu-slayer, do they attain the greatness of you who are so esteemed;
neither your heroism, O Indra, nor your bounty.
Those seers of old and those who are now, O Indra, the inspired poets who have generated sacred prayers—may your auspicious friendships be with us. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
The sacred hymns have risen up, seeking glory; O Vasiṣṭha, magnify Indra in the assembly.
He who has extended all things with his might—may he listen to the words of one such as me.
This cry has been raised, O Indra, born of the gods, as you rule over the spoils in the contest;
for among men one does not perceive his own allotted span of life—so carry us across these very straits.
I harness the booty-seeking chariot with the two bay steeds; my prayers have reached him who delights in them.
Indra, having slain the Vṛtras without opposition, forced asunder those two worlds by his greatness.

Even the waters have swelled like barren cows; O Indra, your singers have reached the sacred Law (*ṛta*). Come toward us as Vāyu with his teams of horses, for through our prayers you distribute the spoils of victory.
May these exhilarating draughts intoxicate you, O Indra, the impetuous one who bestows abundant wealth upon the singer.
For you alone among the gods take pity on mortals; O Hero, rejoice at this libation.

Thus do the Vasiṣṭhas honor Indra, the bull whose arm wields the thunderbolt, with their hymns of praise. May he, being lauded, grant us wealth in heroes and cattle; and may you all protect us always with your blessings.

A seat has been prepared for you, O Indra, in this dwelling; come to it with your men, O much-invoked one! So that you may be our protector for our prosperity, bestow riches upon us and rejoice in the Soma juices.
Your mind has been captured, O Indra of double strength; the Soma is pressed, the sweet juices are poured out.
This well-fashioned hymn, with its released flow of speech, brings praise as this inspired thought loudly calls upon Indra.
From heaven and from earth, O drinker of the *ṛjīṣa*, come to this sacred grass (*barhis*) to drink the Soma!
Let your bay horses carry you toward me, toward our song of praise, you who are powerful, for the exhilaration of the draught.
Come to us with all your aids, O Lord of Bay Horses, being well-pleased and enjoying our prayer; turning toward us with your steadfast ones, O fair-cheeked Indra, bestow upon us manly vigor.
This hymn has been offered to the great and fierce one for his vehicle, like a racing steed striving for the prize.
O Indra, this song of praise seeks you; bestow upon us renown that reaches even to heaven, as if placing a sky above the sky.
Thus, O Indra, fill us with what is desirable; may we find your great favor.
Swell the nourishment rich in heroes for our patrons; protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra, your greatness is indeed great, O fierce one, when the armies, sharing a common purpose, encounter one another.
Let the lightning bolt fall from the arms of the hero; let not your mind wander away in all directions.
O Indra, strike down our enemies in the difficult straits—those mortals who assail us. Drive that curse of the reviler far away; bring us a gathering of riches.

A hundred aids are yours, O fair-cheeked one, for Sudās; let there be a thousand blessings and let your bounty be ours. Strike down the weapon of the mortal who seeks to harm us; bestow upon us splendor and treasure.
For I belong to one such as you in wisdom, O Indra; I belong to one such as you, O Hero, for the sake of protection and bounty.
Make every day a home for me, O fierce one, powerful and rich in bay horses; do not neglect me.
These Kutsas have offered strength to Indra, the lord of bay horses, seeking god-sent power.
O Hero, make the Vritras easy to slay; as conquerors, may we win the prize.
Thus, O Indra, fill us with what is desirable; may we find for ourselves your great favor.
Swell the nourishment rich in heroes for our patrons; and do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
Unpressed Soma has never exhilarated Indra, nor have pressed juices without prayer pleased the Bounteous Lord.
Therefore, I generate a hymn that he may enjoy—a newest song, manly in spirit—so that he may hear us.
At every hymn, Soma has exhilarated Indra; at every chant, the pressed juices have gladdened Maghavan.
When, pressing him closely like sons their father, those of one mind invoke him for protection.
He performed those deeds, and he shall surely perform others now, which the wise proclaim during the libations.
Like a single common husband with his wives, Indra has brought all the fortresses under his control.
Thus they speak of him, and Indra alone is heard of as the distributor of riches, the swift victor whose many aids come one after another; may he bestow upon us his auspicious and beloved favors.
Thus does Vasiṣṭha praise Indra at the soma-pressing, for the sake of aid, him who is the bull among men and the peoples.
Bestow upon us thousandfold spoils; and do you gods protect us always with your blessings.
Men invoke Indra at the turning-point of the rite, so that they may harness those prayers which lead to the further shore.
O Hero, desiring power in the battle for men, grant us a share in the stall rich in cattle.
O Indra, Maghavan, whatever strength is yours, bestow it upon your friends, the many-invoked one, for the sake of these men;
for you, O Maghavan, are the wise dispeller of firm obstacles—open up the wealth that is enclosed as if by a gate.

Indra is the king of the world and of the peoples upon the earth; whatever exists in its manifold forms, from that he bestows riches upon the donor. May he, being praised, even now impel his bounty hitherward.
Now indeed, may the bounteous Indra, when invoked together with us, bestow strength upon us for his aid—
he whose perfect sacrificial fee has overflowed with desirable wealth for the men, his friends, who have sought it out.
Now, O Indra, grant us wide space for the sake of wealth; may we turn your mind toward us for the sake of bounty.
Desiring cattle, horses, and chariots, [we approach you]; do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra, come to us as a wise Brahman; let your bay steeds be harnessed and turned hither toward us. For all mortals indeed invoke you; hear us, O you who pervade all things!
O Indra, your greatness has reached our invocation, since you, O mighty one, protect the sacred prayer (*brahman*) of the seers.
When you, O fierce one, take the thunderbolt in your hand, being terrible yet invincible, you have been born with your will.
Under your guidance, O Indra, you have brought together the two worlds like men who call upon you;
for he was born for great dominion and power, and the impetuous one has impelled even the non-impetuous.
O Indra, be gracious to us through these days, for the peoples who act as ill-disposed friends are being purified.
May the guileful Varuṇa, who perceives the falsehood that has been committed against us, release us from it twofold.

We would speak to this Maghavan Indra, so that he may grant us great wealth and bounty—[to him] who is most helpful to the prayerful singer of the sacred word. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
This Soma, O Indra, is pressed for you; come hither, O Lord of Bay Steeds, for that is your home.
Drink of this well-pressed, pure draught; being entreated, O Maghavan, bestow riches upon us.
O Heroic Brahman, enjoying this creation of prayer, come swiftly hither with your bay steeds;
at this very libation, rejoice, and listen to these our prayers.
What satisfaction do you find in our hymns? When indeed, O Maghavan, shall we serve you?
I have stretched out all my thoughts toward you; therefore, O Indra, hear these my invocations.
And indeed, those men of old were truly yours, of whom you heard, the ancient seers;
therefore, O Maghavan, I invoke you repeatedly—you, O Indra, are our providence, like a father.

Let us address this Maghavan Indra, so that he may grant us great wealth and bounty; he who is the most helpful protector of the one who praises him and performs sacred prayer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O God, come to us with power, O impetuous one; be the increaser, O Indra, of this wealth.
For the sake of great manly valor, O Lord of Men, wielder of the good thunderbolt; for the sake of great dominion and heroic might, O Hero.
The heroes call upon you, the one to be invoked, in the clash of battle for their own bodies and for the winning of the sun;
you are the one to be honored by all people as the leader of armies; do you, who are easy to strike, bring the Vṛtras under our control.
O Indra, when the days dawn with fair weather, and when you raise the foremost banner in battles,
Agni sits down like a divine Hotṛ-priest, summoning the gods here for the sake of prosperity.
O Indra, O Hero, we and those gods who praise you while bestowing gifts—grant to our patrons the highest protection; may they, being self-sustaining, attain long life.

Let us address this Maghavan Indra, so that he may grant us great wealth and bounty; he who is the most helpful protector of the one who praises him and offers prayer. And do you, O gods, protect us always with your blessings.
O friends, sing forth a gladdening song for Indra, the lord of the bay horses, the drinker of Soma.
O bounteous ones, let us recite the hymn of praise, just as men have done for you who dwell in heaven, so that we may act for the sake of him whose wealth is true.
O Indra, you are the seeker of booty for us; O Śatakratu, you are the seeker of cattle;
O Vāsas, you are the seeker of gold.
O Indra, O Bull, we who are devoted to you cry out to you;
know this of us, O Vasu.
Do not deliver us to reproach or to the censure of the stingy enemy;
for my mental power is centered in you.
O slayer of Vṛtra, you are a wide-spreading armor and a warrior who fights from the front;
with you as my ally, I speak in reply.
And you are great, O Indra, whose conquering power the two self-dependent worlds, heaven and earth, acknowledge.
May that voice, accompanied by the Maruts, encompass you—
moving along with us and reaching toward the days of light.
The upward-tending drops have followed you, the wondrous one, to the sky;
the people bow down together before you.
Bring forth [hymns] for the great one who increases greatness; offer your devotion to the wise one. O you who fill the people, advance toward the many clans.
For the far-reaching, mighty Indra, the inspired poets have generated a well-fashioned prayer and a sacred formulation;
the wise do not violate his ordinances.
The voices have established Indra, whose fury is unsurpassed, as the king for all time, so that he may prevail;
strengthen the allies for the sake of the Lord of the Tawny Steeds.
Let not even the priests detain you far from us;
come to our feast even from afar, or, being here, listen to us.
For these prayers, fashioned by the priest, sit with thee at the pressed juice like bees upon honey;
the singers, desiring wealth, have placed their desire in Indra as one places a foot upon a chariot.
Desiring wealth, I call upon the wielder of the thunderbolt, the one with the excellent right hand, as a son calls upon his father.
These Soma juices, mixed with curds, have been pressed for Indra;
come, O wielder of the thunderbolt, to these for exhilaration and for your drink, with your two bay steeds, to your own dwelling.
Hearing us, he whose ears are attentive comes for our wealth; may he never neglect our songs.
He who bestows hundreds and thousands at once—no one can restrain him when he wishes to give.
That hero, irresistible, has flourished through Indra and through men— he who,
O slayer of Vṛtra, presses out your deep libations and pours them forth.
O Maghavan, be the protection for our wealthy patrons when you encounter the defiant;
may we share in the possession of him whom you have struck down. Bring us wealth, O you who are difficult to overcome.
Press the Soma for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the drinker of Soma;
cook the cooked offerings for his protection. Truly, he who gives bestows joy upon the giver.
Do not falter, O Soma-pressers; be skillful for the great purpose. Make yourselves ready to win wealth.
Only the one who perseveres conquers, dwells securely, and prospers; the gods do not aid the one who is stingy.
No one has obstructed the chariot of Sudās, nor has anyone made it halt;
he whom Indra protects and the Maruts accompany—he shall reach a stall full of cattle.
May that mortal win the prize who strives for the prize, O Indra, for whom you have become a protector. Be the protector of our chariots, O Hero, and of our men.
Now his portion overflows like the wealth of a victor;
he who is Indra, the lord of the bay horses, cannot be harmed by enemies—he bestows skill upon the Soma-presser.
Bestow upon those worthy of sacrifice a mantra that is unimpaired, well-placed, and beautiful;
even many snares cannot overcome him who stands by Indra through his ritual action.
O Indra, what mortal would dare to challenge him who has you as his protector?
O Maghavan, through faith alone in you, the prize-seeking warrior strives to win the prize on the decisive day.
In the slayings of Vṛtra, urge on those bountiful ones who bestow beloved wealth;
under your guidance, O Lord of Tawny Steeds, may we, together with our patrons, cross over all difficulties.
Thine, O Indra, is the lowest wealth; thou nourishest the middle;
truly, thou rulest over all that is highest; no one holds thee back from the cattle.
You are renowned as the giver of wealth to everyone; whatever battles there may be, they belong to you.
O Much-invoked One, this entire earthly world, seeking your help, begs for your name.
O Indra, if I were the lord of as much wealth as you possess, I would surely provide for my singer; O bestower of riches, I would grant him nothing to poverty.
May I strive to grant wealth to the one who magnifies me day after day, wherever he may be found;
for there is no kinship better than yours, O Maghavan—not even a father.
The one who crosses over desires to win the prize with Purandhi as his ally;
I bend Indra, the much-invoked, toward you with my song, just as a carpenter fashions a well-rolling wheel-rim.
A mortal does not find wealth through ill-praise; riches do not reach the one who falters.
O Maghavan, you alone possess the power to grant a gift like yours on the decisive day.
We cry out to you, O Hero, like unmilked cows, to you, O Indra,
the lord of this moving world, the beholder of heaven, the lord of all that stands still.
None other like you exists—neither among the dwellers of heaven nor upon earth; none has been born, nor shall be born.
O bountiful Indra, we who long for horses and yearn for cattle, we call upon you as those seeking strength.
Bring that wealth here for us, O Indra, [taking] from the younger [man] what is greater;
for you, O Maghavan, have been rich in many treasures from of old, and are to be invoked in every battle.
Drive away our enemies, O Maghavan; make riches easy for us to find. Be our protector in the great contest for wealth; be the increaser of your friends.
O Indra, bring us wisdom, just as a father provides for his sons. Teach us, O much-invoked one, on this journey; living, may we attain the light.
Let not unknown, malevolent, or unpropitious powers step upon us.
O Hero, with your aid we shall cross over the many flowing rivers.
White-robed, with their hair-knots on the right, the inspirers of prayer have indeed gladdened me;
rising from the sacrificial grass, I say to the men: "The Vasiṣṭhas are not far off to protect me."
From afar they brought Indra with the pressed juice, past the Vaiśanta pool, beyond the fierce drinker.
From the pressed soma of Pāśadyumna Vāyata, Indra chose the Vasiṣṭhas.
Verily, with these [Maruts] he crossed the river; verily, with these he struck down Bheda.
Verily, O Vasiṣṭhas, it was through your sacred prayer that Indra protected Sudās in the battle of the ten kings.
O men, through the sacred prayer (*brahman*) of your fathers, you have attained favor; your axle has not worn out, nor indeed have you suffered harm.
For when you Vasiṣṭhas, with a loud roar, sang the *śakvarī* verses, you bestowed strength upon Indra.
Like thirsty men gazing up at heaven, they, being hemmed in during the battle of the ten kings, looked out in their distress;
Indra heard Vasiṣṭha as he offered praise, and he made wide space for the Tritsus.
Like sticks, the Bharatas were cut down like cattle-herds, they being small and weak;
but Vasiṣṭha became their leader, and then the tribes of the Tṛtsus spread abroad.
Three create seed within the worlds; three are the noble offspring, whose forefront is light.
Three heats attend the Dawn; all these the Vasiṣṭhas know.
Their radiance is like the growth of the sun; their greatness is as profound as the ocean;
their speed is like that of the wind—O Vasiṣṭhas, your hymn of praise cannot be equaled by any other.
By means of the perceptions of their hearts, they move toward that secret which has a thousand branches;
weaving the enclosure spread out by Yama, the Vasiṣṭhas have approached the Apsarases.
When Mitra and Varuṇa beheld you emerging from the lightning’s light,
that was one of your births, O Vasiṣṭha— namely, when Agastya brought you forth for the clans.
And you, Vasiṣṭha, are the son of Mitra and Varuṇa, born from the mind of Urvaśī, O Brahman;
all the gods received you as a fallen drop by means of divine prayer within the lotus.
He, the perceiver who knows both worlds, the giver of thousands or indeed of all gifts—
Vasiṣṭha was born from the Apsarases as he was about to weave the enclosure stretched out by Yama.
Born at the sacrifice, impelled by adorations, the two poured forth their common seed into the jar;
from its midst Māna arose, and therefore they call the seer born therefrom Vasiṣṭha.
He who bears the bearer of hymns and the bearer of chants, bearing the pressing-stone, speaks forth first.
Approach him with well-disposed minds; Vasiṣṭha, the piercer, shall come unto you.
May the divine inspired thought, well-fashioned by us, go forth from us like a swift chariot.
They know the origin of the earth and of heaven; the waters listen as they flow.
Even the broad waters swell for him; in the midst of the Vṛtras, the fierce heroes consider themselves mighty.
Place the horses at his yoke-poles, like Indra the wielder of the thunderbolt with golden arms.
Like a charioteer setting out for a sacrifice, like a traveler on his path, urge yourselves forward by your own power.
By your own power, further the sacrifice in battles; establish a banner, a hero for the people.
From his vital strength the light has emerged; it bears its burden as the earth bears the ground.
O Agni, free from sorcery, I invoke the gods; accomplishing [my purpose] through the Eternal Law (ṛta), I fashion this prayer.
Direct your divine thought toward us; send forth your speech among the gods.
Varuṇa, the fierce one with a thousand eyes, beholds the path of these rivers.
King of kingdoms, ornament of rivers, may he extend his sovereign power over all life.
Protect us in all communities; make the curse of the one who seeks to harm us ineffective.
Let the malevolent missile of our enemies fly away; drive off in every direction the affliction that harms our bodies.
May Agni carry our oblations with our reverences; this most beloved hymn has been offered to him.
In harmony with the gods, make the Son of the Waters our friend; may he be auspicious to us.
With hymns I praise the serpent born from the waters, who sits at the base of the rivers in the mid-regions.
May the serpent of the deep not deliver us to harm; may the sacrifice of this seeker of truth not fail.
And may they bestow renown upon these our men; may the arrogant enemies go forth for wealth.
They scorch the enemy like the sun upon the earth; these ones possess great armies and [overpower] them with their terrors.
When our wives come hither, may Tvaṣṭṛ, the skillful-handed, bestow upon us heroic sons.
May Tvaṣṭṛ accept our hymn; may Aramati, seeking wealth, be with us.
May they, the bestowers of gifts, grant us riches; may Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, providing excellent refuge with his protectresses, be our benefactor and bestow wealth upon us.
May the mountains grant us that wealth, may the waters, the plants that accompany the gifts, and the sky grant it;
may the earth in harmony with the trees of the forest, and both heaven and earth, protect us on every side.
May the two vast worlds, heaven and earth, yield to that; may Varuṇa, dwelling in the heavens and having Indra as his friend, yield;
and may all the Maruts, who are full of power, yield. May we be the ones to establish a foundation for wealth.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the waters, the plants, and the trees take pleasure in that.
May we be in the protection and the lap of the Maruts. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
May Indra and Agni be auspicious to us with their protections; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are offered, be auspicious to us.
May Indra and Soma be for our well-being, for peace, and for health; may Indra and Pūṣan be auspicious to us in the winning of booty.
May Bhaga be auspicious to us, and may our praise be auspicious; may Purandhi be auspicious to us, and may riches be auspicious.
May the praise of truth that is easily governed be auspicious to us, and may Aryaman, born of many, be auspicious to us.
May the Ordainer be auspicious to us, and may the Sustainer be auspicious to us; may the far-reaching [Earth] be auspicious to us with her self-sustaining powers.
May the two great worlds, Heaven and Earth, be auspicious, may the mountain be auspicious to us, and may the propitious invocations of the gods be auspicious to us.
May Agni, with his face of light, be auspicious to us; may Mitra and Varuṇa and the Aśvins be auspicious to us.
May the good deeds of the doers of good be auspicious to us; may the swift wind blow auspiciously upon us.
May Heaven and Earth be auspicious to us at our first invocation; may the mid-air be auspicious for our sight.
May the plants and the trees be auspicious to us; may the victorious Lord of the atmosphere be auspicious to us.
May the god Indra with the Vasus be auspicious to us; may Varuṇa, the one of fair praise, with the Ādityas be auspicious.
May the cooling Rudra with the Rudras be auspicious to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the divine dames hear us here for our welfare.
May Soma be auspicious for us; may the sacred prayer be auspicious for us; may the pressing-stones be auspicious for us, and may the sacrifices be auspicious.
May the felling of the sacrificial posts be auspicious for us; may the plants be auspicious for us, and may the altar be auspicious.
May the far-seeing Sūrya rise for our welfare; may the four quarters of space be auspicious for us.
May the steadfast mountains be for our well-being, and may the rivers and the waters be auspicious for us.
May Aditi be auspicious to us through her sacred laws; may the Maruts, who sing beautiful hymns, be auspicious to us.
May Viṣṇu be auspicious to us, and may Pūṣan be auspicious to us; may our protection be auspicious, and may Vāyu be auspicious to us.
May the divine Savitṛ, our protector, be auspicious to us; may the dawns as they shine forth be auspicious to us.
May Parjanya be auspicious to our progeny, and may the Lord of the Field be a source of well-being to us.

May the All-Gods be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī, together with our prayers, be auspicious. May those who accompany us be auspicious, and may those who grant gifts be auspicious; may the divine ones, the earthly ones, and those of the waters be auspicious to us.
May the lords of truth be auspicious to us; may our coursers be auspicious and our cattle be auspicious.
May the Ṛbhus, the skillful-handed doers of good deeds, be auspicious to us; may the Fathers be auspicious to us in our invocations.
May the divine Aja Ekapād be auspicious to us; may Ahi Budhnya be auspicious to us, and may the Ocean be auspicious.
May Apām Napāt, the protector, be auspicious to us; may Pṛśni, whose guardians are the gods, be auspicious to us.
May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus take pleasure in this newly performed prayer;
may those who dwell in heaven, those on earth, those born of the cow, and those worthy of sacrifice hear us.

Those who among the gods are worthy of sacrifice, who are the most worshipful of those worthy of worship, who are the objects of Manu's veneration, immortal, and knowers of the *ṛta*—may they grant us wide-striding space today; and may you protect us always with your blessings.
Let the sacred prayer proceed from the seat of Cosmic Order; Sūrya has released the cows with his rays.
The wide earth has spread out with her ridges; Agni has been kindled upon her broad surface.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, O Asuras, I fashion this newest hymn for you both like nourishing food;
one of you is a powerful, unerring leader on the path, while the other, speaking as Mitra, stirs the people.
The arrivals of the gliding wind have come to rest; like milch-cows, the sweet juices have overflowed. Being born in the seat of the great heaven, the bull has bellowed in this very udder.
O Indra, with my song I have yoked these two bay steeds of yours, which are dear to you, well-charioted, heroic, and swift.
May I bring hither the wise Aryaman, who subdues the wrath of the one who seeks to harm us.
Worshipers pay homage in their own abode of *ṛta* to his friendship and vital strength; praised by men, he has distributed nourishments. This most beloved homage is for Rudra.
When the glorious ones, lowing together, come—Sarasvatī, the seventh, whose mother is the Sindhu;
they who flow well, easy to milk, with good streams, swelling with their own milk.
And may those Maruts, being exhilarated, protect our prayer, our offspring, and our strength;
O swift ones, let not the moving syllable pass us by, for they have increased our appropriate wealth.
Bring forth for yourselves the great Aramati; bring forth Pūṣan like a hero worthy of the assembly.
Bring forth Bhaga, the protector of our prayers, and Purandhi, who bestows gifts and wins strength in the acquisition of this [wealth].

O Maruts, may this song of praise reach you, and may it reach Viṣṇu, the protector of the infused seed, with your aids. And may you bestow vigor upon the progeny and upon the one who sings your praises. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Vājās and Ṛbhukṣans, may your most swift and unassailable chariot bring you here to be praised.
At the libations, with Soma-pressings upon the three ridges, fill yourselves with joy, O fair-cheeked ones, through your great exhilarations.
O R̥bhukṣans, you who behold the light of heaven, you bestow unimpaired treasure upon the liberal patrons;
O self-dependent ones, drink together at the sacrifices and distribute riches to us through our prayers.
For you have granted gifts, O Maghavan, in the distribution of wealth, both great and small;
both your hands are full of riches, and your benevolence does not withhold treasures.
O Indra, you are self-glorious, a lord of the *Ṛbhus*, like a successful prize; come home as one accompanied by hymns.
May we, the Vasiṣṭhas, now be your givers, performing sacred prayer for you, O Lord of the Bay Steeds.
You shall win even from the heights for the donor, with those prayers by which you, O Lord of the Bay Horses, have exerted yourself;
we have indeed won through your allied aids. When, O Indra, will you grant us wealth?
O Indra, you seem to make us, the wise ones, dwell [in your presence]; when will you take notice of our speech?
May the swift steed, through our ancestral prayer, bring us wealth consisting of heroic sons and nourishing food to our home.
Even though the goddess Nirṛti herself rules over him, may many prosperous autumns come to Indra;
may he, with his threefold kinship, reach old age, even though mortals have made him homeless.
O Savitṛ, may gifts be praised for us; may the riches of Parvata come to us in their bounty.
May the divine protector always attend to us. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings.
Upward has this god Savitṛ extended the golden radiance which he has sent forth;
now indeed is Bhaga to be invoked by men, he who, possessing abundant wealth, distributes treasures.
Arise, O Savitṛ, and hear this, O golden-handed one, at the presentation of the sacred rite (*ṛta*).
Spreading forth your wide and vast splendor, bestow upon men the food that sustains mortals.
May the god Savitṛ be praised, whom even all the Vasus extol;
may he, worthy of homage, accept our hymns with favor and protect our patrons with all his guardians.
Him whom the goddess Aditi praises, delighting in the impulse of the god Savitṛ;
him whom Varuṇa, the sovereign, and the Mitras and Aryaman praise in unison.
May those who, vying with one another, bestow gifts from heaven and earth—those who share in the giving—and may Ahi Budhnya hear us; may Varūtrī protect us along with the Ekadhenu cows.
May the Lord of the Family, being entreated, grant us that treasure of the god Savitṛ.
The mighty one calls upon Bhaga for protection; even the weak man seeks Bhaga and attains his treasure.
May the Vājins be auspicious to us in our invocations during the service of the gods—those who run with measured pace, who sing beautiful songs;
may they, crushing the serpent, the wolf, and the demons, drive away all diseases far from us.
In every contest for booty, O Vājins, protect us—you who are wise, immortal, and knowers of the *ṛta*—in the distribution of wealth.
Drink of this honeyed mead and rejoice; satisfied, go by the paths traveled by the gods.
Agni, standing erect, has sent forth his favor toward wealth; his glowing flame goes forward toward the assembly of the gods.
The two pressing-stones have taken their path like chariot-drivers; may the Hotṛ-priest, impelled, sacrifice for us according to the Eternal Law (Ṛta).
The sacrificial grass, easy to tread upon, has been spread out for them; like two lords of the people, they come to the assembly.
At the first invocation of the night and of the dawn, may Vāyu with his team and Pūṣan come for our well-being.
O Vasus, here on earth the gods have taken delight; the brilliant ones have adorned themselves in the wide mid-air.
O you of broad strides, turn your paths hitherward; hear this messenger of ours who has come.

For they, the worshipful protectors worthy of sacrifice, all the gods, occupy their common dwelling place. O Agni, at this rite, sacrifice to those who desire it—with prompt obedience—to Bhaga, the Nāsatyas, and Purandhi.
O Agni, from heaven and from earth, bring hither Mitra, Varuṇa, Indra, and Agni;
bring Aryaman, Aditi, and Viṣṇu among them; may Sarasvatī and the Maruts rejoice.
May the insatiable one reach the oblation of the worshipful ones with our prayers, fulfilling the desire of mortals;
may he grant us wealth that is never-failing and ever-conquering. May we now indeed be accompanied by the yoked gods.
Now may Rodasī, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—the upholders of Ṛta—be praised by the Vasiṣṭhas.
May these radiant ones grant us our most excellent hymn. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
May the readiness for the assembly come together; let us offer our praise to the swift ones.
Whatever the god Savitṛ shall impel today, may we be present at his distribution of treasures.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, the two worlds (Heaven and Earth), Indra, and Aryaman grant us that wealth allotted by the gods;
may the goddess Aditi assign us riches, as well as Vāyu and Bhaga, whom they yoke together.
O Maruts, let that mortal be fierce and powerful whom you, whose horses are dappled, protect;
and whom Agni and Sarasvatī impel—for him there is no one who can surpass his wealth.
For this Varuṇa is the leader of the *ṛta*, and Mitra, Aryaman, and the Waters are kings; the goddess Aditi is easy to invoke and invincible. May they carry us across distress, remaining unharmed.
At the offering of oblations to this bounteous god Viṣṇu, the swift one, may we find the Rudra-like majesty of Rudra; O Aśvins, come to our food-providing dwelling.
O Pūṣan, glowing one, let not the envious Varūtrī nor those who accompany the gifts withhold them from us.
May the joy-bringing coursers protect us; may the wind, wandering all around, grant us rain.
Now may Rodasī, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—the upholders of Ṛta—be praised by the Vasiṣṭhas. May the radiant ones grant us this most excellent hymn. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
At dawn we invoke Agni; at dawn Indra; at dawn Mitra and Varuṇa; at dawn the Aśvins;
at dawn Bhaga, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati; at dawn let us invoke Soma and Rudra.
Let us invoke the fierce Bhaga, the winner of the morning, the son of Aditi who is the distributor;
him whom even the weak-minded man, even the swift one, and even the king say, "May I partake of Bhaga."
O Bhaga, leader; O Bhaga, whose gifts are true; O Bhaga, favor this prayer and grant us wealth.
O Bhaga, increase us with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, may we be rich in men through our heroes.
And may we now be fortunate, both at the onset of the day and at its midday;
and at the rising of the sun, O Maghavan, may we abide in the benevolent favor of the gods.
O gods, let Bhaga alone be the blessed one; through him may we become possessed of fortune. O Bhaga, everyone invokes you; as such, O Bhaga, be our leader here.
May the Dawns incline toward our sacrifices; like Dadhikrāvan, they hasten toward the pure place.
May they bring hither to us Bhaga, the finder of wealth, as spirited horses draw a chariot.
May the auspicious Dawns, rich in horses, cows, and heroes, shine upon us forever. Yielding clarified butter and overflowing from every side, do you protect us always with your blessings.
Let the Brahmans and the Aṅgirases come forward; let the roar of the celestial thunder-cloud arise.
Let the milk-cows swimming in the waters low; let the two pressing-stones be yoked, the ornament of the sacrifice.

O Agni, your path is easy to traverse, discovered from of old; yoke for the pressed juice your bay and ruddy horses, or those ruddy steeds that carry heroes to the seat. Seated there, I invoke the generations of the gods.
I celebrate your sacrifice together with prostrations; the joyous Hotṛ-priest has surpassed [all others] nearby.
O you of many faces, worship the gods well; may you turn hither the holy Aramati.

When Agni, the guest who lies on a comfortable bed, is made manifest in the dwelling of the wealthy hero; when he is well-pleased and well-established in the house, he bestows desirable wealth upon such a people.
O Agni, enjoy this sacrifice of ours; make it glorious for us among the Maruts and Indra.
Let Night and Dawn sit upon the sacred grass; worship Mitra and Varuṇa here as they desire.
Thus has Vasiṣṭha, desiring wealth that nourishes all, praised the victorious Agni. May he extend to us food, riches, and strength; and may you all protect us always with your blessings.
At your sacrifices, those seeking the gods sing forth with adorations to Heaven and Earth so that they may grant us nourishment—
those for whom the peerless prayers of the inspired singers spread out in all directions like the branches of a tree.
Let the sacrifice proceed like a swift horse toward its goal; lift up with one mind the ladles dripping with ghee.
Strew the sacred grass well for the rite; the god-seeking flames have risen upward.
Like sons borne upon their mother's lap, may the gods sit upon the back of the sacred grass. May the all-pervading goddess anoint the assembly; O Agni, do not neglect us in the service of the gods.
Those worshipful ones have been gratified according to their pleasure, milking the well-yielding streams of *ṛta*.
Today, come with one mind to your supreme greatness among the Vasus, as many as you are.

Thus, O Agni, bestow upon us among the people; through you, O possessor of power, may we be closely united. May we, together with our companions, rejoice in wealth and remain unharmed. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
For your protection, I invoke Dadhikrā first, the Aśvins, Uṣas, the kindled Agni, and Bhaga;
Indra, Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, the Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Sun.
Awakening Dadhikrā with reverence, rising up and proceeding toward the sacrifice,
seating the goddess Iḷā upon the sacrificial grass— let us, as inspired singers, invoke the Aśvins who are easily summoned.
Awakening Dadhikrāvan, Agni, the Dawn, the Sun, and the Cow, and the ruddy,
brown one of the wrathful Varuṇa— may they all drive away every misfortune from us.
Dadhikrāvan, the first prize-winning steed, goes at the head of the chariots, knowing the way;
he is in harmony with the Dawn, with Sūrya, with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aṅgirases.
May Dadhikrā anoint our path so that we may follow the way of *ṛta*;
may the divine host Agni hear us, and may all the mighty, unerring ones hear us.
May the god Savitar, possessor of beautiful jewels, come through the mid-air, borne by his horses; holding many gifts for men in his hand, he settles the world and impels it forth.
His two arms, supple and vast, golden-hued, have reached to the ends of heaven. Surely that majesty of his is to be praised; even the Sun yields to him in active power.
May that god Savitṛ, the powerful one, the lord of treasures, impel treasures for us. Spreading his far-reaching radiance, may he now bestow upon us the food that sustains mortals.
These songs praise Savitar, the fair-tongued one, whose arms are full and whose hands are skillful.
May he bestow upon us wonderful and lofty vital strength. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Bring these songs to Rudra, the god who possesses a firm bow, swift arrows, and self-sustaining power;
to the invincible, the conqueror, the wise ordainer, the wielder of sharp weapons—may he hear us.
For he, through his dominion over earthly birth and his sovereignty over celestial birth, takes heed of us.
O Rudra, come toward our protecting doors with favor; be one who is free from disease among our offspring.
That bolt of yours which, released from heaven, moves across the earth—may it spare us.
O you who drink the sweet draught, you possess a thousand remedies; do not harm us among our children or grandchildren.
Do not slay us, O Rudra, do not abandon us; let us not fall into the snare of your wrath.
Grant us a share in the sacred grass and in the praise of the living. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Waters, that wave of yours which those seeking the gods first made into the drink of Indra— may we today win from you that pure, stainless, honey-sweet wave which sprinkles clarity with ghee.

O Waters, may that wave of yours which is most rich in sweetness—may Apāṃ Napāt, the swift impeller, protect it—that wave in which Indra rejoices with the Vasus; may we, seeking the gods, attain it from you today.
Flowing through a hundred purifiers, rejoicing with the *svadhā* offering, the goddesses go to the domain of the gods.
They do not violate the laws of Indra; offer an oblation rich in ghee to the rivers.
Those which Sūrya has stretched out with his rays, those for whom Indra carved a path and a wave—may you, O rivers, grant us wide space; and may you protect us always with your blessings.
O R̥bhukṣans, O Vājas, O heroes, you bounteous ones, rejoice in our pressed soma!
May your powers, like those who come hitherward, turn your mighty, manly chariot toward us.
May we, as Ṛbhu with the Ṛbhus, be masters over you; as Vibhū with the Vibhūs, may we overcome powers with power.
May Vāja aid us in the winning of booty; with Indra as our ally, may we overcome Vṛtra.
For they indeed overcome many with their command; Indra, Vibhvan, R̥bhukṣan, and Vāja, subduing every hostile power, shall by their conflict shatter the manly strength of the enemy foe.
Now, O gods, grant us wide space; may you all, being of one mind, be present for our protection.
May the Vasus bestow nourishment upon us; do you ever protect us with your blessings.
Led by the ocean, purifying themselves from the midst of the waters, they flow on without resting;
those divine waters which Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, dug out—may they protect me here.
The waters that are celestial, or those that flow [on earth], whether dug out or self-born;
those whose goal is the ocean, pure and purifying—may those divine waters protect me here.
In whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men—those dripping with sweetness, pure, and purifying; may those divine waters protect me here.
In whom King Varuṇa, in whom Soma, and in whom all the gods revel in vigor;
in whom Agni Vaiśvānara has entered—may those divine waters protect me here.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect me here; let not the all-pervading, nest-making [evil] come upon us.
I have warded off the ill-seeing goat-footed one; let not the creeping thing find me with its foot-sore disease.
