Whatever splinter has become lodged in the joint of the limb, or whatever reaches from the knee-caps down to the ankles—may Agni, shining brightly, drive that away from here; let not the shafting disease find me with its foot.

Whatever poison is in the *śalmali* tree, whatever is in the rivers, and whatever is born from the plants—may all the gods drive that away from here; let not the creeping worm find me with foot-infecting disease.

Those rivers which flow down, those which flow up, those which flow out, those which are full of water, and those which are waterless—may all those divine waters, swelling with milk for us, be auspicious and free from disease; may all the rivers be free from the *śimidā* affliction.

Through the newest protection of the Ādityas, through their most peaceful shelter, may we prevail. May the swift ones, listening to us, establish this sacrifice in sinlessness and in the state of Aditi.
May the Ādityas and Aditi rejoice; may Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, who are most upright, be our guardians of the world. May they drink the Soma today for our protection.
O Ādityas, all the Maruts, all the gods, and all the Ṛbhus;
Indra, Agni, and the Aśvins, being praised—do you all protect us ever with blessings.
O Ādityas, may we be free from bonds; O Vasus, may we be secure among the gods and among mortals.
Winning, O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we win; being present, O Heaven and Earth, may we be present.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, our guardians, grant us this protection for our children and descendants. May we not suffer for the sin committed by another; O Vasus, let us not do that which you punish.
The swift Aṅgirases, imploring it, have obtained the treasure of the god Savitṛ.
May our great father and all the gods, being of one mind, graciously accept this from us as worthy of sacrifice.
With sacrifices and prostrations, I fervently invoke the great, worshipful Heaven and Earth;
for those ancient seers, singing their praises, established these two mighty ones, the parents of the gods, in the forefront.
Bring forward the two first-born parents with newest songs in the seat of Cosmic Order.
O Heaven and Earth, come to us with the divine host; great is your protective shelter.
For indeed, O Heaven and Earth, you possess many treasures for the liberal giver;
bestow upon us that which may be unfailing. Protect us always with your blessings.
O Lord of the Dwelling, recognize us; be one who grants us easy entry and be free from disease for us.
Whatever we implore of you, favor that with us; be a blessing to our bipeds and a blessing to our quadrupeds.
O Vāstoṣpati, be our furtherer; O Indu, increase our household with cattle and horses. May we remain unaging in your friendship; favor us as a father favors his sons.
O Vāstoṣpati, may we be united with your auspicious, delightful, and path-finding assembly.
Protect our welfare both in rest and in exertion; and do you all protect us always with blessings.
O Vāstoṣpati, dispeller of disease, entering into all forms,
be a most gracious friend to us.
O Sārameya, O Arjuna, since you bark, O tawny one,
like gleaming spears in their scabbards as they devour, fall fast asleep!
O Sārameya, you bark at the thief or the robber, O you who come back again;
yet you bark at the praisers of Indra—why do you seek to trouble us? Go to sleep!
Pierce the boar; let the boar pierce you! You roar at the praisers of Indra—why do you seek to bring us misfortune? Go to sleep!
May the mother sleep, may the father sleep; may the dog sleep, may the lord of the household sleep.
May all kinsmen sleep, and may this person around us sleep.
Whoever sits, whoever moves about, and whoever looks at us—
of them we shall strike down the eyes, just as we have struck down this dwelling.
The bull with a thousand horns who has risen up from the ocean— with him, the powerful one, we lull the people to sleep.
The women who lie on couches, those who lie on beds, those who dwell upon their mattresses,
and those women who possess auspicious fragrances— all of them we cause to sleep.
Who are these men, clearly manifest, dwelling in the same nest, the youths of Rudra, who possess noble horses?
For no one knows their births; they alone know each other's place of origin.
They have sown themselves with their own purities; roaring like the wind, the falcons have contended with one another.
The wise one discerned these secret things, that Pr̥śni, the great one, bore them in her udder.
May that clan, through the Maruts, be rich in heroes, eternally victorious, and increasing its manly strength.
They who are most swift in their course, most beautiful in splendor, endowed with glory, and fierce in their vital powers.
Terrible is your might, steadfast are your powers; thus, with the Maruts, the host is powerful.
Bright is your breath, wrathful are your minds; like a roaring sage, you are the impetuous leader of the bold host.
Keep your missile far away from us; let not your ill-will reach us here.
I invoke the dear names of you, the swift ones, so that you, O Maruts, may be satisfied and respond with longing.
Well-armed, impetuous, wearing beautiful breastplates, they adorn their own bodies themselves.
Pure are the oblations for you, O Maruts, who are pure; I present the pure sacrifice to the pure ones.
By the Eternal Law (ṛta), those who are true to the Law have come—the pure-born, the pure, the purifiers.
Upon your shoulders, O Maruts, are your rings; golden ornaments rest upon your chests.
Shining like lightning with rain, you wield your weapons according to your own nature.
Your great splendors from the depths arise; O you who are worthy of sacrifice, extend your names.
O Maruts, accept this thousandfold domestic portion, this offering of the householder.
O Maruts, if you should take heed of this praise offered at the invocation of the inspired singer who seeks strength,
then quickly grant us wealth with noble heroes— wealth which no other stingy enemy can ever harm.
Like swift horses, the Maruts are self-moving; like youths visible to the seer, they have adorned themselves for beauty.
Established in their mansions, bright as calves, they play about like young offspring, dispensers of milk.
May the Maruts, bestowing gifts upon us, be gracious; may they, making the two well-established worlds wide for us, be merciful.
Let your weapon that slays cattle and men be far away; O Vasus, incline toward us with your favors.
The Hotṛ-priest, having sat down and praising you, O Maruts, repeatedly invokes your all-encompassing bounty.
He who is such a protector as this, O Bulls, being free from duplicity, calls upon you with hymns.
These Maruts bring the swift one to rest; they bend down force by force. They protect the praise from the one who seeks to harm it, and they bestow heavy hatred upon the stingy one.
O Maruts, you rouse even the weakling, just as the Vasus take pleasure in the swift one;
O Bulls, drive away the darkness and bestow upon us all our progeny and offspring.
O Maruts, let us not be excluded from your gifts; let us not be left behind when you, the chariot-borne ones, distribute your wealth.
Grant us a share in that desirable riches which is well-born and yours, O heroes.
When the people, as heroes, clash together with their wrath over the great rivers, the plants, and the settlements—
then, O Maruts, sons of Rudra, be our protectors in the battles against the enemy.

O Maruts, you have performed many deeds for our fathers; those hymns of praise which are recited for you even from of old—through the Maruts, the fierce one is victorious in battles; through the Maruts, the steed wins the prize.

O Maruts, may there be among us a heroic and vigorous man, a lord who is the sustainer of people, by whom we may cross over the waters for a secure dwelling; may we then abide in our own home under your protection.
May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Agni, the waters, the plants, and the trees take pleasure in this.
May we be under the protection and in the lap of the Maruts. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.

O worshipful ones, your Marut-host is like honey; they rejoice with power at the sacrifices, they who cause even the two wide worlds to tremble and fill the spring when they have gone forth as the fierce ones.
For the Maruts are the observers of the one who praises them, and the furtherers of the sacrificer’s prayer.
Today, at our assemblies, sit upon the sacred grass for the feast, being well-pleased.

Other Maruts do not shine so much as these do with their golden ornaments, weapons, and bodies; adorning both heaven and earth, they, adorned with every ornament, apply a common unguent for the sake of beauty.
May that bolt of yours, O Maruts, be far from us when we have committed any offense against you through human frailty.
O worshipful ones, let there be no share for us in that [wrath]; may your most gracious favor be with us.
Even when this is done, O Maruts, may you who are blameless, pure, and purifying take delight;
protect us with your benevolent thoughts, O worshipful ones, and further us with your strengths so that we may prosper.
And may the Maruts, being praised, come to our oblations with all their names, O heroes!
Grant us a portion of immortality for our progeny; bestow upon us wealth and bounteous gifts of truth.
O Maruts, being praised, come hither with all your aids toward our patrons for complete success—those who themselves increase us by hundreds. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
Sing forth to the host that sprinkles together, the mighty one of the divine abode;
they stir heaven and earth with their greatness and reach the firmament from the depth of destruction.
Even from their very birth, O Maruts, you are fierce in your splendor—terrible, impetuous in wrath, and tireless.
Those who by their greatness and power stand forth; at your approach, every beholder of the light trembles with fear.
Bestow great vital strength upon our patrons; may the Maruts graciously accept our fair praise. As a traveled path leads a person forward, may he advance us with desirable aids.
Favored by you, O Maruts, the inspired singer wins a hundredfold; favored by you, the victorious steed wins a thousandfold.
Favored by you, even the sovereign king slays Vṛtra; let that gift of yours be ours, O shakers of the world.
I seek to win over those [Maruts] who belong to the bounteous Rudra; will the Maruts not turn toward us again?
Whatever they have been angry with us for in secret or openly, we pray for that forgiveness from those swift ones.

This fine hymn of praise has been uttered for the liberal patrons; may the Maruts take pleasure in this well-spoken song. O bulls, drive away our enemies even from afar! Do you protect us always with your blessings.
O gods, him whom you protect here and there, and him whom you lead—
grant him protection, O Agni, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, and Maruts.
O gods, by your protection on the day of battle, the one who sacrifices dear to you overcomes his enemies;
he extends his dwelling and increases great nourishments—he who gives to you according to your desire.
For Vasiṣṭha does not despise even the last among you;
O Maruts, all of you who desire it, drink today at our pressed soma.
For your aid does not fail in battles for him to whom you have granted it, O heroes;
may your newest favor turn toward us—come quickly, O ye who desire to drink!
O impetuous ones, come quickly to these offerings for the drinking of the soma-juice;
O Maruts, I have presented these oblations to you—do not go elsewhere!
Sit upon our sacred grass and be our protectors, so that you may grant us desirable wealth.
O Maruts, never failing in your purpose, rejoice here in the sweet Soma juice; Svāhā!
Even the swans with dark-blue backs, adorning their bodies, have flown hither;
the entire host has settled down all around me, like joyful men rejoicing at the libation.
O Maruts, O Vasus, whoever with evil intent seeks to strike us down, transgressing our thoughts—may he be caught in the snares of his own malice; slay him with your most scorching blow!
O Maruts, you who are the Sāṃtapanas, may you graciously accept this oblation; come to us with your aid, O destroyers of enemies!
O Maruts, you who dwell in the home, come hither; do not stay away from us, O bounteous givers, for your protection.
O Maruts, you who are self-strong, poets with sun-bright skins, I choose your sacrifice here and now.
We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant one who increases prosperity;
may I be liberated from death, as a cucumber from its stem, yet not from immortality.
O Sūrya, when you rise today as one free from sin, speak the truth for the sake of Mitra and Varuṇa. O Aditi, may we be dear to you among the gods, O Aryaman, as we sing your praises.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, this Sūrya, the observer of men, rises up over both worlds upon the earth;
he is the guardian of all that is stationary and all that moves, beholding the upright among mortals and the crooked as well.
He has harnessed from their station the seven tawny mares, dripping with ghee, who carry Sūrya.
Devoted to you both, O Mitra and Varuṇa, he surveys all beings as if they were herds.
Up have risen for you both the nourishing draughts rich in sweetness; Sūrya has ascended the bright flood, he for whom the Ādityas—Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa acting in harmony—prepare his paths.
For these—Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa—are indeed the perceivers of abundant falsehood;
they have increased in the dwelling-place of Truth, the capable sons of Aditi, who are undeceivable.
These—Mitra and Varuṇa, who are difficult to deceive—awaken even the mindless with their skillful powers. Bestowing wise intention upon them, they lead them by good paths even across distress.
These vigilant ones of heaven and earth lead the mindless on;
even in the rushing of the rivers there is a ford. May they carry us across this perilous strait.
The auspicious protection that Aditi, Mitra, and Varuṇa, like guardians, extend to Sudās—
placing our children and grandchildren within it, O swift ones, let us not commit any offense against the gods.
May he worship at the altar with oblations; may Aryaman ward off all those who harm and are upheld by Varuṇa. O Bulls, may he encompass the wide space for the liberal giver, Sudās, from all enmities.
For even the encounter with these [Maruts] is like that of horses; by their secret power they prevail through their fierce might.
O Bulls, trembling in fear of you, show us mercy by the greatness of your skill.
He who wins the favor of the priest for the sake of gaining strength and the highest wealth—
those liberal lords subdue the wrath of the enemy and have prepared a wide, well-established dwelling for their habitation.
O Gods, Mitra and Varuṇa, this priestly service has been performed for you both at the sacrifices.
Carry us across all difficulties; protect us always with your blessings.
Upward rises your eye, O Varuṇa, the fair-faced one of you two gods; Sūrya goes forth, spreading his light.
He who beholds all living beings—he has taken notice of the fury among mortals.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, this inspired sage, faithful to the *ṛta*, offers you prayers that reach far; whose sacred hymns you two, O wise ones, protect, so that through his wisdom you may fulfill the autumns as if with your own power.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two, the bounteous givers, have placed your spies throughout the wide earth, from the lofty and vast heaven,
and among the plants and the people, watching with unblinking eyes in every direction.
Praise the domain of Mitra and Varuṇa; their impetuous strength has firmly established the two worlds by its greatness.
May the months of those who do not sacrifice pass away without heroes; may he who is mindful of sacrifice extend his own stronghold.

O unerring bulls, all these things of yours are manifest; in them no marvel is seen, nor any secret power. The deceptions and falsehoods of men attend them, yet no hidden mysteries have remained concealed from you two.

I magnify your sacrifice together with reverent salutations; I call upon you, Mitra and Varuṇa, with earnest devotion. May these new prayers of mine be proclaimed for recitation; may you graciously accept these offered hymns.
O Gods, Mitra and Varuṇa, this priestly service has been performed for you both at the sacrifices.
Carry us across all difficulties; protect us always with your blessings.
The Sun has extended his lofty rays over all the many generations of men. Shining, he has become visible as one with heaven; fashioned by the makers with wisdom, he has become well-fashioned.
He has risen toward the sun like a fortress before us, with these hymns, by means of these swift, dappled steeds.
Proclaim us as sinless before Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, and Agni.
May the upholders of *ṛta*—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—bestow upon us a thousandfold riches.
May the radiant ones grant us a hymn worthy of praise; may they, being lauded, fulfill our desire.
O Heaven and Earth, O Aditi, protect us—you who were born of noble lineage by those who brought you forth, O lofty ones.
May we not incur the wrath of Varuṇa, nor that of Vāyu, nor of Mitra, who is most dear to men.
Stretch forth your arms that we may live; sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter.
O youthful ones, make us famous among the people; hear these my invocations, O Mitra and Varuṇa.
Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant us freedom for ourselves and for our offspring.
May all our ways be easy to traverse and our paths be fair; do you protect us always with your blessings.
The fortunate Sūrya, the all-seeing, rises up as the common possession of mankind—
the god who is the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa, and who has rolled up the darknesses like a skin.
Up rises the impeller of men, the great banner of Sūrya, surging like the sea;
he who, yoked at the pole, draws Etaśa as he seeks to turn the single wheel around.
Radiant from the lap of the dawns, he rises up being celebrated by the singers;
this god Savitṛ has pleased me—he who does not violate the common law.
The golden ornament of heaven, far-seeing, rises up—the swift traveler, shining across the distance.
Now indeed, impelled by Sūrya, let the people go forth to their goals and perform their works.
Where the immortals have made a path for him, he follows that course like a hawk swooping down;
at the rising of the sun, we shall worship you both, O Mitra and Varuṇa, with prostrations and oblations.
Now may Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman grant wide space for ourselves and for our offspring. May all our ways be easy to traverse and our paths be fair. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
Dwelling in heaven and upon the earth across the mid-air, may they present for you both the robes of clarified butter.
May Mitra, Aryaman, and the noble-born King Varuṇa of goodly power graciously accept our oblation.
O Kings, guardians of the great cosmic order, lords of the rivers, you two Kṣatriyas, come hither! O Mitra and Varuṇa, bestowers of swift gifts, send down nourishment for us and rain from heaven.

May Mitra, Varuṇa, and the divine Aryaman lead us forward by the most effective paths, so that the enemy may speak [of our deeds] to Sudās; thus, protected by the gods, may we rejoice in nourishment together.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may he who has fashioned this seat for you with his mind, and who makes and sustains this upright prayer—sprinkle him with clarity, O Kings; satisfy those well-settled dwellings.
This hymn, O Varuṇa and Mitra, is offered to you like bright Soma to Vāyu. Favor our prayers, awaken our abundant thoughts; do you protect us always with your blessings.
At the rising of the sun, I invoke you both with hymns— Mitra and Varuṇa of pure will—
whose divine power is imperishable and supreme, who move swiftly, watching over all on their journey.

For they are the *asuras* among the gods, they are the noble ones; may you two make our dwellings full of strength. O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we attain you both where the heavens and the days cause [all things] to swell with abundance.
Those two are the bridges of falsehood with many snares, difficult for a mortal enemy to overcome.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, may we cross over misfortunes by your path of Truth, as one crosses waters by means of a boat.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our offering with oblations of clarified butter and with nourishing gifts;
for the sake of the people here, grant them their desire and bestow upon them the delightful waters of heaven.
This hymn, O Varuṇa and Mitra, is offered to you like bright Soma to Vāyu. Favor our prayers, awaken our abundant thoughts. Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
Let our powerful hymn of praise go forth to Mitra and Varuṇa, accompanied by homage, toward those two of mighty birth.
Those gods who, highly skillful and sons of Dakṣa, uphold [the world] with great majesty for the sake of divine power.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, you who protect our bodies and guard us like lords of the dwelling, fulfill the prayers of those who sing your praises.
When today at the rising of the sun, Mitra, Aryaman,
Savitṛ, and Bhaga impel us to be sinless.
May that dwelling be well-protected; may those who give good gifts now go forth on their journey, they who carry us across distress.
And also those self-ruling Adityas who, being undeceived, rule over the great ordinance as kings.
At the rising of the sun, I sing praise to you both, Mitra and Varuṇa,
and to Aryaman, the destroyer of enemies.
Through wealth of gold, may this prayer bring unassailable power; may this inspired singer [bring it] for the winning of the prize.
May we be yours, O divine Varuṇa, and yours, O Mitra, together with our patrons; may we obtain nourishment and well-being.

Many are they who have the sun as their eye, Agni as their tongue, and who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*); they who, through their insights, have directed the three assemblies, and through their all-encompassing powers, [direct] all things.
Those who have established the year, the month, and the day, as well as the sacrifice, the night, and the verse—
Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman, the kings, have attained unattainable sovereignty.
This we meditate upon for you today with hymns at the rising of the sun—that which Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman favor; you are the charioteers of the Eternal Order (ṛta).

O you who are true to the cosmic order (*ṛta*), born of the cosmic order, increasing the cosmic order—terrible ones who hate untruth! In your favor, which provides the most secure protection, O heroes, may we and those who are our wise patrons abide.
Up rises that beautiful form at the turning-point of heaven,
which the swift divine Etaśa draws, sufficient for all to behold.
The Lord of all that moves and stands, who dwells throughout the entire expanse of space—
seven sister bay mares carry Sūrya in his chariot for our well-being.
May that eye, established by the gods, the bright one rising upward, enable us to see for a hundred autumns; may we live for a hundred autumns.
O undeceivable Varuṇa and Mitra, come with your poetic wisdom, radiant ones, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Varuṇa and Mitra, come with the powers of heaven, you who are free from guile;
drink the Soma, O impellers!
Come hither, O Mitra and Varuṇa, accepting the oblation, O heroes; drink the Soma, you who increase the cosmic order.

O lords of men, with a sacrificial mind possessed of oblations, I shall praise your chariot so that it may come hither—your chariot, O you who are worthy of the altar, which has awakened like a messenger; I call out to you as a son calls to his parents.
The kindled fire has shone for us; even the ends of darkness have become visible.
The banner of the Dawn has been perceived in the east, born for the glory of the Daughter of Heaven.
O Aśvins, Nāsatyas, the eloquent and skillful invoker now attends you with hymns;
come hither by many pathways on your light-finding, treasure-laden chariot.
O Aśvins, desiring you, I now call upon you both with devotion when the sweet juice is pressed, seeking wealth, O lovers of honey.
Let your sturdy horses carry you hither; drink the well-pressed mead among us.

O divine Aśvins, make my forward-striving prayer fruitful for the winning of wealth; protect all our inspired thoughts in the quest for booty. O Lords of Power, assist us with your powers so that you may enable us.
O Aśvins, protect us in these prayers; may our seed be prolific and free from shame.
Striving for offspring and descendants, may we, possessing fine jewels, go to the feast of the gods.
This treasure has been placed for you two in friendship, like one sent ahead, O lovers of sweetness;
it is bestowed upon us. Come hither with a mind free from anger, eating the oblation among the human clans.

In a single course, O swift ones, upon the same path, your chariot has gone around the seven flowing rivers. The well-formed, god-yoked steeds do not weary, they who, being swift, carry you at the poles.
Be unfailing toward the liberal patrons who, with their wealth, incite the giving of gifts;
they who further their kin through noble deeds, bestowing riches in cattle and horses.
Now hear my invocation, O youthful ones; come, O Aśvins, on your path rich in nourishment.
Bestow treasures and grant long life to our patrons; protect us always with your blessings.
Come hither, O bright Aśvins, with your noble horses, you wonder-workers who take pleasure in the songs of your devotee;
enjoy our oblations that have been presented.
The intoxicating juices have been set forth for you; come readily to enjoy my oblation.
Hearing us, pass over the invocations of the enemy.
O Aśvins, your chariot, swift as thought and providing a hundredfold protection, speeds forth across the regions for us, O you who possess the wealth of Sūryā, as it is entreated.
When this stone, seeking the gods, presses upward for you two as it extracts the Soma, may the inspired sage turn hither with oblations, O beautiful ones.
Truly, that wondrous nourishment which you possess— bestow it upon Atri, who is full of power,
he who, being dear to you, places his trust in your protection.
And that deed of yours, O Aśvins, was for the aging Cyavāna, who offered the oblation—
a deed worthy of being remembered— when you bestowed upon him a new form through your protection.
Moreover, O Aśvins, those evil-minded friends abandoned that Bhujyu in the midst of the ocean; but he who was devoted to you delivered him from it, O givers of no gifts.
You gave strength even to the exhausted Vṛka; O Aśvins, being invoked, you were heard by Śayu.
Just as you made the cow swell with water, so too, O Aśvins, by your powers, you strengthened even the barren woman through your wondrous deeds.
This very singer, awakened at the break of dawn with well-spoken hymns, praises him with a devout mind.
May the inviolable cow increase his strength with food and milk. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
May your golden chariot, pressing against heaven and earth, come hither with its stallions;
gleaming with its fellies, with tracks of clarified butter, it is the bearer of refreshments, the lord of men, and rich in prize-winning steeds.
Spreading over the five worlds, let him who has three seats go forth, yoked by the mind—
by whom you two go to the people seeking the gods, O Aśvins, taking whatever course you will.
Come hither with your noble horses, O Wondrous Ones; drink the honeyed treasure.
Your chariot, moving with the bride, presses against the ends of heaven with its two tracks.
The daughter of the Sun chose your splendor for herself during the night's departure;
when you two protect the one seeking the gods with your powers, the bird goes around the heat through your protection.

O chariot-borne ones, that very chariot of yours which, yoked, goes its circuit while the dawn breaks— thereby, O Aśvins, bring us well-being and security at the dawning of the dawn to this sacrifice.
O Heroes, like thirsty bulls seeking the lightning, come today to our libation. For in many places they invoke you with their prayers; let not other seekers of the gods restrain you.
O Aśvins, you two carried Bhujyu, who was cast down into the ocean, out from the waters with your unfailing, winged, tireless, and unswerving steeds, delivering him by means of your wondrous powers.
Now hear my invocation, O youthful ones; come, O Aśvins, on your nourishing path.
Bestow treasures and grant long life to our patrons; protect us always with your blessings.
O Aśvins, possessors of all boons, come to us! This place upon the earth has been proclaimed for you.
Like a prize-winning horse with a smooth back, he has stood ready; come, sit down as if upon a fixed womb.

May that most delightful benevolence attend you both; even the sacrificial vessel (gharma) is heated within the house of man—he who brings you across the oceans and rivers, yoking his chariot as if with well-harnessed, swift steeds.

O Aśvins, those places which you establish in the great waters of heaven, in the plants, and among the people; you sit upon the summit of the mountain, bringing nourishment to the person who offers oblations.
O Gods, you have rejoiced in the plants and in the waters when you obtained the ritual tasks of the seers.
Bestowing many treasures upon us, you have looked back over the ancient ages.

O Aśvins, though you have already heard of many things, you look upon the sacred prayers (*brahmāṇi*) of the seers. Come forth toward the choice of the people; may your most excellent benevolence be with us.

O Nāsatyas, to whatever sacrifice of yours there may be—provided with oblations, accompanied by sacred hymns, and contested—come forward to Vasiṣṭha according to your choice; these prayers are being chanted for you both.

This is the inspired thought, this is the song, O Aśvins; may you, O bulls, take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn. May these prayers, longing for you, reach you. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
The sister departs from her sister, Dawn; the dark one yields the path to the ruddy one.
We invoke you two, who bring wealth in horses and wealth in cattle; day and night, keep the arrow away from us.
Come to the mortal who offers oblations, O Aśvins, bringing desirable wealth upon your chariot;
drive away from us lack of nourishment and disease; O lovers of sweetness, protect us by day and by night.
May the bull-like [Maruts], seeking your favor, bring your chariot hither at the first flush of dawn;
O Aśvins, with horses yoked by the Eternal Law and reins held in hand, bring your wealth-laden chariot!
O lords of men, that chariot of yours which is the bearer, three-seated, wealthy, and swift as the dawn—
come to us with it, O Nāsatyas, when the one who provides for all comes toward you.
You two released Cyavāna from old age; you brought the swift horse to Pedu.
You delivered Atri from distress and darkness, and you placed Jāhuṣa within a secure refuge.

This is the inspired thought, this is the song, O Aśvins; may you, O bulls, take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn. May these prayers, longing for you, reach you. Do you protect us always with your blessings.
Come, O Nāsatyas, on your chariot rich in cattle, rich in horses, and most resplendent;
all our teams attend upon you, as you shine with a lovely splendor in your bodies.
Come toward us with the gods, O Nāsatyas, being of one accord on your chariot;
for our friendship with you is ancestral, our kinship is common—be mindful of that.
The hymns of praise for the Aśvins have awakened; the kinship of the sacred prayers and the divine Dawns has been stirred.
Seeking to win over the two worlds, these inspired singers call upon the Nāsatyas.
When the dawns shine forth, O Aśvins, the singers bring their prayers to you;
the god Savitṛ has sent his light upward, and the fires sing aloud with kindled fuel.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come from behind, from the front, from below, and from above; come from every side with wealth that belongs to the five peoples. Do you ever protect us with your blessings.
We have crossed to the further shore of this darkness, offering our hymn of praise, seeking the gods.
The song calls upon the Aśvins—the doers of many deeds, the most abundant, the ancient, the immortal ones.
The beloved priest of man has indeed sat down, O Nāsatyas, he who sacrifices and offers praise.
Eat of the honeyed draught, O Aśvins, nearby; I, providing the sacrificial food, call upon you in the assemblies.
We have prepared the sacrifice, choosing the broad paths; O Bulls, may you take pleasure in this well-fashioned hymn.
Like one sent with a ready ear, Vasiṣṭha has awakened for you with songs of praise, chanting your names.

May those two carriers come near to our people, O slayers of demons, you who are joined together and have strong hands. The intoxicating juices have gathered; do not neglect us, but come with your auspicious favor.
O Nāsatyas, O Aśvins, come from behind, from the front, from below, and from above; come from every side with wealth that belongs to the five peoples. Do you ever protect us with your blessings.
These morning sacrifices call you, O Aśvins, at the break of dawn.
I here invoke you for protection, O Lords of Might, for you go to every tribe.
O Heroes, you two have bestowed wondrous nourishment; impel it toward the one who possesses the truth.
With one mind, bring your chariot hither and draw near; drink the Soma-sweetness.
Come hither, attend to us, and drink of the honeyed draught, O Aśvins!
You have milked the milk, O bulls, possessors of noble wealth; do not neglect us, but come!
The horses that carry you both fly toward the house of the donor;
O Aśvins, heroes, with those swift steeds, come to us, O gods, seeking us.
Then indeed, as they go forth, O Aśvins, the wise patrons attend upon you with nourishing food.
May those two Nāsatyas grant enduring glory and a secure dwelling to our generous patrons and to us.
Those who have gone forth like chariots, free from predators, protectors of men;
those heroes have increased by their own power and they dwell in secure habitation.

Uṣas, born of heaven, has shone forth according to the Eternal Law (ṛta); manifesting her majesty, she has come. She has driven away the hated darkness of the malevolent; best of the Aṅgirases, she has awakened the paths.
Awaken us today for great prosperity; O Uṣas, lead us forward toward great good fortune.
Bestow upon us, O divine and human goddess among mortals, wonderful wealth that brings glory and is worthy of renown.
These, those very rays of the beautiful Dawn, the immortal and brilliant ones, have arrived;
engendering the divine ordinances and filling the mid-air, they have spread abroad.
Yoking her chariot from afar, she swiftly traverses the five lands;
surveying the works of men, she is the daughter of Heaven and the mistress of the world.
Possessing abundance, the daughter of the Sun, of wondrous wealth, she rules over riches and treasures.
Praised by the seers, awakening the world, the bountiful Dawn shines forth, extolled by the priests.
The ruddy horses, bright and radiant, have appeared, carrying the Dawns toward us.
She comes, the brilliant one, on her chariot adorned with every ornament; she bestows treasure upon the person who honors her.

True with the true, great with the great, a goddess with the gods, worthy of sacrifice with those worthy of sacrifice—she breaks open the firm places and bestows the ruddy cows; the cattle lowed toward the Dawn.
O Uṣas, now bestow upon us wealth consisting of cattle, heroes, and horses—abundant nourishment for us.
Do not let our sacrificial grass be exposed to contempt among men. And do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Savitar, the god who belongs to all men, has extended the immortal light that is common to all.
Through the power of the gods, the Eye was born; Uṣas has made the entire world manifest.
The paths leading to the gods have appeared before me, tireless and prepared by the Vasus.
The banner of the Dawn has indeed arisen in the east; she has come hither from the heights of the firmament.
Those were indeed many days that lay before the rising of the sun, since then,
O Uṣas, you have been seen appearing like a lover, as if never having departed before.
They were the companions at the banquet of the gods, the upholders of *ṛta*, the ancient seers;
as fathers, they discovered the hidden light and, with true mantras, brought forth the Dawn.
United upon the same wide expanse, they are in harmony and do not strive against one another;
they do not violate the ordinances of the gods, for they move together with the Vasus, never failing.
The Vasiṣṭhas, awakening at dawn, praise thee with hymns, O fortunate one, having offered their laudations.
Leader of the kine, mistress of booty, shine upon us; O nobly born, be the first to awaken.
This leader of bounty and of pleasant truths, Dawn, shining forth, is praised by the Vasiṣṭhas;
bestowing upon us wealth renowned afar, do you all protect us ever with your blessings.
She has shone forth like a young maiden, impelling all that lives to movement;
Agni has appeared for the kindling of men, creating light and driving away the darkness.
Facing all things, she has risen far-extending; wearing a radiant garment, she has shone with brilliant white.
Golden-hued, beautiful to behold, mother of the cows and leader of the days, she has gleamed.
The blessed Dawn has appeared, the eye of the gods, carrying along and leading forth the white horse so beautiful to behold;
radiant with her rays, she shines with wonderful wealth, spreading over the entire world.
Drive away the enemy far from us; make for us a wide pasture free from fear.
Ward off those who hate us, bring us riches, and bestow bounty upon the one who praises you, O Maghavan.
O Goddess Uṣas, shine upon us with your most excellent rays, prolonging our lifespan.
Bestowing nourishment upon us, O possessor of all boons, grant us wealth consisting of cattle, horses, and chariots.
O Uṣas, daughter of heaven, well-born one, whom the Vasiṣṭhas magnify with their hymns—you, bestow upon us vast and lofty wealth. And may you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
The first rays have become visible; her upward-reaching banners spread abroad.
O Uṣas, with your great, radiant chariot, bring us desirable wealth from the near side.
Agni, well-kindled, awakens to greet her; the sages, praising with their hymns, greet her in turn.
The goddess Uṣas approaches, driving away all darkness and misfortunes with her light.
These very Dawns have appeared in the east, bestowing light as they shine forth.
They have brought forth the sun, the sacrifice, and the fire; the hated darkness has departed to the west.
The wealthy Daughter of Heaven has been perceived; all behold the Dawn as she shines forth.
She has mounted her chariot, which is yoked by its own inherent power—the chariot which well-yoked horses draw.
May our liberal patrons and we ourselves awaken toward you today with well-disposed minds. O Dawns, as you shine forth, be full of abundance for us. Protect us always with your blessings!
Dawn has revealed the paths of men, awakening the five human settlements.
With her well-beheld oxen she has spread forth her radiance; Sūrya has opened heaven and earth with his sight.
They anoint the nights at the ends of heaven; like people who have harnessed their teams, the dawns strive forward.
Your cows, O Night, roll up the darkness and extend the light, as Savitṛ extends his arms.
The Dawn has appeared, most like Indra, the bounteous; she has brought forth glories for our well-being.
The daughter of Heaven, the goddess, best of the Aṅgirases, distributes treasures to the doer of good deeds.
O Uṣas, grant us as much bounty as you bestowed upon those who praised you when you were lauded;
you whom they brought forth with the roar of a bull, you opened the firm doors of the mountain.
Impelling every god toward bounty, sending forth our truthful words, dawning upon us to win our prayers—grant us these! Do you all protect us evermore with your blessings.
With hymns of praise and songs, the Vasiṣṭhas, the inspired poets, were the first to awaken to greet Uṣas,
who causes the two regions at the ends of the world to revolve and reveals all living beings.
Bestowing new life upon us, Uṣas has awakened, having concealed the darkness with light;
the youthful maiden goes forth unabashed, and she has made manifest the sun, the sacrifice, and Agni.
May the auspicious Dawns, rich in horses, cows, and heroes, shine upon us evermore. Yielding clarified butter and overflowing on every side, do you protect us always with your blessings.
The daughter of Heaven has been seen approaching, shining forth;
she uncovers the great waters so that we may see, and the noble lady creates light to dispel the darkness.
The sun, rising together with them, releases the radiant rays; he rises as the shining constellation.
O Dawn, at your dawning and that of the sun, may we attain a share of his bounty.
O Dawn, daughter of heaven, we have awakened for you,
the swift one— you who, O bountiful goddess, bring much that is desirable, like treasure, as joy to the donor.
O Great Goddess, as you shine forth, you bestow greatness so that we may behold the light of heaven;
as such, we, partaking of your treasures, entreat you: may we be like sons to our mother.
O Dawn, bring us that wondrous wealth which is most far-famed;
O Daughter of Heaven, grant us that food for mortals which you possess, so that we may enjoy it.
May she grant immortal fame to our patrons, wealth consisting of cattle, and booty rich in kine to us.
May Uṣas, the impeller of the wealthy and full of pleasantness, dawn away our enemies.
O Indra and Varuṇa, grant great protection to our sacrifice, to our people, and to our clan.
May we, victorious in battles, overcome those who seek to harm us and the evil-minded.
One of you is called the sovereign king, the other the self-ruling lord; O Indra and Varuṇa, you two are great and possessors of great wealth.
All the gods in the highest heaven have bestowed upon you both, O bulls, vital energy and strength.
By your might you dug out the channels of the waters and set the sun, the lord, in heaven;
O Indra and Varuṇa, in the exhilaration of this wondrous draught, you caused the waterless places to swell and you made our prayers overflow.
In battles and in conflicts, the priests bring you both; for the attainment of security, those with firm-kneed steeds invoke you both.
O Indra and Varuṇa, masters of both kinds of wealth, we poets, easy to call upon, invoke you.
O Indra and Varuṇa, when you two created all these beings of the world by your might,
Mitra honors Varuṇa with peace, while the other, the fierce one, goes forth with the Maruts for glory.

For the sake of Varuṇa’s great prize, they indeed measure out his own steadfast power and brilliance. One [of the two] overcomes the unrelated one who seeks to harm; the other, with few means, prevails over many.

Neither distress, nor misfortunes, nor suffering from any quarter, O Indra and Varuṇa, shall reach that mortal, whose sacrifice you two gods go to and enjoy; no treachery of a mortal shall overcome him.
Come hither, O heroes, with divine protection; hear my call if you take pleasure in it.
For the friendship and the kinship that you possess, O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow your compassion upon us.
O Indra and Varuṇa, in every battle be our foremost warriors with your power over the people, when both sides invoke you in the struggle, as men do for the winning of offspring and progeny.

May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman bestow upon us splendor and great, far-reaching protection. We meditate upon the unassailable light of Aditi, the praise of the god Savitṛ, who increases the cosmic order.
Beholding you two, O heroes, as our kinsmen, men seeking cattle with broad axes have marched forward.
Slay both the Dāsa and the Ārya enemies; O Indra and Varuṇa, protect Sudās with your aid.
Where men gather together with raised banners, in that battle where there is nothing at all pleasant,
where all beings tremble before those who behold the light of heaven— there, O Indra and Varuṇa, speak for us!
The dust-clouds have covered the ends of the earth; O Indra and Varuṇa, the shout has risen to heaven.
The hostilities of the people have come near me; hear my call with your protection and come hither!
O Indra and Varuṇa, with irresistible weapons, you conquered Bheda and protected Sudās.
You heard their prayers at the invocation; thus the priestly service of the Tṛtsus became effective.
O Indra and Varuṇa, the hostilities of the enemy and the enmities of our rivals press hard upon me.
For you two rule over the wealth of both worlds; therefore, protect us on the decisive day.
Both sides invoke you two in the battles—Indra and Varuṇa—for the winning of wealth;
when Sudās was hard-pressed by the ten kings, you aided him together with the Tṛtsus.
Ten kings assembled together, who were not performers of sacrifice, did not prevail against Sudās, O Indra and Varuṇa.
The praise of these men seated at the feast proved true; the gods were present for them during their invocations of the gods.
O Indra and Varuṇa, you bestowed aid upon Sudās when he was surrounded on all sides by the ten kings;
there, where the Tṛtsus, white-robed, wearing their hair in braids, and full of devotion, worshipped you with homage and prayer.
One of you strikes down the Vṛtras in battles; the other ever guards the sacred laws.
We invoke you both, O mighty ones, with well-fashioned hymns; O Indra and Varuṇa, grant us protection.

May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman grant us splendor and great, far-reaching protection. We meditate upon the unassailable light of Aditi and the song of the god Savitṛ, who increases the cosmic order.
O Kings Indra and Varuṇa, may I turn you both toward this sacrifice with oblations and salutations.
The ladle, filled with clarified butter, held in our arms, goes forth by itself toward you who possess diverse forms.
The vast realm of heaven promotes your sovereignty, you who bind with fetters that require no ropes.
May you turn away from us the wrath of Varuṇa; may Indra make for us a wide world.
Make our sacrifice dear in the assemblies; make our prayers praiseworthy among the patrons. May wealth impelled by the gods come to us; further us with your desirable aids.
O Indra and Varuṇa, bestow upon us wealth that possesses all desirable things, abounding in riches and many cattle.
He, the Āditya, who destroys falsehoods, the hero, distributes boundless treasures.
May this song of mine reach Indra and Varuṇa; may it protect us, urging us on toward offspring and progeny.
Possessing fine jewels, may we go to the feast of the gods. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
I purify for you both a hymn free from demons, offering Soma to Indra and Varuṇa—like the goddess Uṣas with her face of ghee. May they two protect us on our journey in the encounter.
They indeed vie with one another here at the invocation of the gods, where amidst the banners the missiles fall.
O Indra and Varuṇa, strike those enemies away with your arrow, scattering them in all directions.
For even the Waters, the goddesses, self-glorious in their assemblies, have established Indra and Varuṇa as deities.
One of them sustains the scattered peoples; the other slays the irresistible Vṛtras.

May he be a wise and truth-perceiving Hotar-priest, who, Adityas, being full of power and reverence, has brought you both here for protection with an oblation; may he, providing nourishment, abide for our well-being.
May this song of mine reach Indra and Varuṇa; may it protect us, striving for offspring and progeny.
Possessing fine jewels, may we go to the feast of the gods. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
By his greatness, the wise one indeed separated the generations, he who propped apart even the two wide worlds;
he pushed up the lofty, high firmament, and twice over established the star and spread out the earth.
And I converse with you regarding that very body; when indeed shall I be within the presence of Varuṇa?
What offering of mine would he accept without anger? When shall I look upon his grace with a well-disposed mind?
I ask about that transgression, O Varuṇa, desiring to see it; I approach the wise to inquire.
Even the sages say one and the same thing to me: "This Varuṇa here is angry with you."

What was the greatest offense, O Varuṇa, that you seek to strike down your praiser, your friend? Declare that to me, O invincible one, self-dependent lord; then, being free from sin, may I quickly approach you with my homage.
Release us from the sins committed by our ancestors, and from those which we ourselves have committed with our own bodies.
O King, release Vasiṣṭha, as one releases a thief who has stolen cattle, or a calf from its tether.
O Varuṇa, that is not one's own skill, but a deception; it is wine, anger, the dice, and thoughtlessness. The elder is present at the side of the younger; even sleep itself does not ward off untruth.
Like a servant for a bountiful master, may I, sinless, do service for the impetuous god. The noble god has enlightened the unenlightened; as a wiser seer, he stirs the wise man toward wealth.
O self-dependent Varuṇa, may this hymn of praise be firmly established in your heart.
May it be auspicious for us in rest and auspicious for us in exertion. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Varuṇa carved out paths for the sun and opened the oceanic channels of the rivers; like a released troop of mares, he, following the cosmic order, made the great channels flow for the days.
Your breath, the wind, has roared through the mid-air like a wild beast eager for pasture after winning its prey;
between these two great and lofty worlds, O Varuṇa, all your beloved domains abide.
The spies of Varuṇa, sent forth by his command, behold both the well-established worlds;
they are the upholders of *ṛta*, the seers wise in sacrifice, the far-sighted ones who further the inspired thought.
Varuṇa spoke to me, the wise one: "The Cow bears twenty-one names.
Knowing the secret places of the station, the inspired sage has not revealed them, desiring to instruct the later age."
Three heavens are deposited within him; three earths are below, forming six divisions.
The wise King Varuṇa has fashioned this golden swing in heaven for his glory.
Varuṇa stands over the Sindhu like the sky; he is like a white drop, a powerful wild beast.
Of profound renown, the measurer of the mid-region, he is the king of this existing world, whose dominion is secure.
May he who shows mercy even to one who has committed an offense—may we be sinless before Varuṇa.
Fulfilling the ordinances of Aditi, may you protect us always with your blessings.
O Vasiṣṭha, present to the bountiful Varuṇa this most beloved hymn,
purified for him who shall bring hither the worshipful, thousandfold-bestowing, mighty bull.

Now, having come into his sight, I consider the face of Agni to be that of Varuṇa. When the Lord of Heaven has brought the light—the food—to me upon the stone, may he lead me to behold his wondrous form.
When Varuṇa and I board the ship and we propel it into the midst of the ocean;
when we move along upon the ridges of the waters, let us swing back and forth on the swing for the sake of glory.

Varuṇa placed Vasiṣṭha upon the ship; the skillful one made him a seer by his mighty powers—the inspired singer, while the days were at their best, as many as the heavens have stretched out and as many as the dawns.
Where have those friendships of ours gone, when we formerly dwelt together in safety?
O self-dependent Varuṇa, I have come to your lofty dwelling, your house with a thousand doors.
O Varuṇa, if a constant friend and beloved comrade should commit offenses against you, may we, though sinners, not suffer for them, O worshipful one; O sage, grant protection to him who praises you.
Dwelling in these firm habitations, may Varuṇa release the noose from us;
winning favor from the lap of Aditi—do you all protect us always with blessings.
O King Varuṇa, may I not go to a house made of clay;
have mercy, O good ruler, have mercy!
When I go forth as if quivering like an inflated leather bag, O wielder of the stone, have mercy, O good ruler; have mercy!
Through my own lack of resolve, O pure one, I have indeed gone against you;
have mercy, O lord of good dominion, have mercy!
Thirst has afflicted your singer who stands in the midst of the waters;
have mercy, O noble ruler, have mercy!
Whatever offense against the divine host we humans commit here, O Varuṇa—
whether through thoughtlessness or by violating your laws— do not harm us for that sin, O God.
The pure, honeyed pressed juices have been offered to you both with manly zeal by the *adhvaryu* priests.
O Vāyu, bring your teams; come hither, drink of the pressed sap for exhilaration.
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure, for you who are the Lord, he who has offered an oblation to you—the pure Soma—makes him famous among mortals; every son born to him is born as a victor.
For the sake of wealth, these two worlds, Heaven and Earth, brought him forth; for the sake of wealth, the divine Dhiṣaṇā establishes the god.
And may his teams of horses attend upon Vāyu, as well as the white one, the bestower of riches, in his preeminence.
The blameless Dawns have dawned with fair days; meditating, they have found the wide light.
The *uśij* have opened even the stall of cattle; following them, the waters have flowed from of old.
They, meditating with a truthful mind and joined by their own purposeful will, draw the chariot that carries heroes; O Indra and Vāyu, lords of all, nourishments attend your chariot.

May those who are lords and bestow light upon us with cattle, horses, treasures, and gold— Indra and Vāyu, as patrons— may they, through their steeds and heroes, prevail in battles throughout our entire life.

Like coursers seeking glory, we Vasiṣṭhas, with excellent hymns, call upon Indra and Vāyu for their aid; desiring strength, we invoke you for our protection. Do you ever protect us with your blessings.
Surely those blameless gods who in the ancient time were strengthened by our homage—
did they not cause Dawn to shine with the Sun for Vāyu and for Manu when he was oppressed?
Desiring us like two messengers, you two guardians are not to be deceived; you protect us through many months and autumns.
O Indra and Vāyu, this well-uttered hymn approaches you; it entreats you for mercy and for new prosperity.
The wise, white one, the glory of his teams, attends those who possess plenteous food and increase their wealth.
They, being of one mind, have stood forth for Vāyu; all these men have secured good offspring.
As far as the vigor of the body, as far as the strength, as far as men perceive with their sight—O Indra and Vāyu, drinkers of the pure, drink the pure Soma among us; sit upon this sacred grass.

Harnessing your teams of horses, O Indra and Vāyu, whose heroes are desirable, come hither in one chariot; for this first portion of the sweet mead has been offered to you. Now, being gratified, unyoke your steeds among us.
O Indra and Vāyu, the hundred teams and the thousand teams that attend you, possessing all desirable things—come hither with those well-disposed teams; O heroes, drink of the offered honeyed mead.
Like coursers seeking glory, we Vasiṣṭhas, with fair praises, call upon Indra and Vāyu; striving for strength, we invoke you for our protection. Do you ever protect us with your blessings.
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure, come to us; yours are a thousand teams, O possessor of all boons.
To you this intoxicating juice is offered, of which, O God, you take the first draught.
The swift presser has stepped forth at the sacrifices to pour out Soma for Indra and Vāyu to drink,
when the god-seeking Adhvaryus bring you the first of the sweet juices with their skillful powers.
O Vāyu, with those teams by which you go forth to the donor for the sacrifice in his home,
bestow upon us wealth that provides excellent nourishment, and grant us a hero, along with the gift of cattle and horses.

May we, with our patrons, be those Vāyu-like winds who exhilarate Indra, who are god-seeking, who strike down the enemy, and who, slaying the *vṛtras*, may we— overpowering our foes in battle with our heroes— be victorious through our leaders.
Come to our sacrifice with your teams of horses, by the hundreds and by the thousands, O Vāyu; rejoice at this libation. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, may you today take pleasure in this pure, newly-born hymn of praise.
For I invoke both of you, who are easily summoned; you two are most capable of bestowing strength instantly upon the one who desires it.
For you two have become winners of booty through your power, growing together and increasing in might;
ruling over wealth and abundant pasture, bestow upon us a full measure of enduring and vigorous strength.
When the inspired singers, seeking wisdom with their prayers, come near to the assembly of the prize-winners—
like racing steeds reaching the goal— those men call aloud upon Indra and Agni.
Seeking protection with his songs, the inspired sage prays for glorious wealth that brings the first share.
O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, wielders of the fair thunderbolt, further us with new gifts.

When the two great ones, contending and vying with each other, radiant in their own bodies, come together for the battle of heroes; then, at the sacrifice, let the god-seeking people utterly strike down the one who seeks not the gods, along with those who press the Soma.
O Indra and Agni, come hither to this pressing of Soma for our goodwill; for you do not disregard us at all. May I turn you both hither with constant offerings of strength.
O Agni, thus kindled by this homage, speak to Mitra, Varuṇa, and Indra;
whatever sin we have committed against them, forgive that, and may Aryaman and Aditi release us from it.
O Agni, may we, aspiring for these offerings, obtain strength through your companionship.
May neither Indra nor Viṣṇu, nor the Maruts, look with disdain upon us. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
O Indra and Agni, this ancient hymn of praise for you has arisen from this thought of mine,
like rain from a cloud.
Hear the caller's invocation, O Indra and Agni; accept our songs.
As lords, cause our prayers to swell with abundance.
O Indra and Agni, do not deliver us to wretchedness, nor to calumny;
do not subject us to the reproach of our enemies.
To Indra and Agni we offer great homage and a well-fashioned hymn; seeking aid, we implore them with prayer and song.
For indeed, the inspired poets, ever pressing forward, thus invoke them for aid,
for the winning of booty.
With songs of praise, we who offer oblations call upon you both,
desiring to win the prize at the sacrifice.
O Indra and Agni, you who subdue the peoples, come to us with your protection; let not the one of evil intent have power over us.
O Indra and Agni, grant us protection; let not the malice of any envious mortal reach us.
O Indra and Agni, may we win that wealth which we implore from you— wealth consisting of cattle, gold, and horses.
When, O Soma, the men have pressed you out, they, the devoted ones, have called upon Indra and Agni,
who possess the pair of steeds.
With hymns, with songs, and with shouts of praise, they seek to win those two who are the greatest slayers of Vṛtra, even when they are already exhilarated.
May those two [Aśvins] strike down the ill-speaking mortal, the evil-minded, the demoniac;
may they strike down the oppressor with their blow, may they strike down the flood with their blow.
With her swelling, nourishing flood, this Sarasvatī has flowed forth; she is a supporting, iron-strong fortress.
Like a chariot, she rushes on, overwhelming all other rivers by her greatness.
Sarasvatī alone among rivers has awakened; pure, she flows from the mountains to the ocean.
Perceiving the wealth of the vast world, she has yielded milk and ghee for the son of Nahuṣa.
He has grown strong among the maidens—the manly, vigorous young bull among those worthy of sacrifice. He bestows a prize-winning steed upon the patrons; may he groom his body for the sake of winning.
And may Sarasvatī, the auspicious one, hear us graciously at this sacrifice;
being entreated by those who bow with joined knees, she—joined with wealth—is superior even to her friends.
Offering these oblations to you with prostrations, O Sarasvatī, accept our hymn of praise. Placing ourselves within your most beloved protection, may we come for refuge as to a tree.

O Sarasvatī, this Vasiṣṭha has indeed opened wide for you the two doors of Cosmic Order, O auspicious one. Prosper, O radiant one; grant riches to the one who praises you. And do you all protect us always with your blessings.
I sing forth a lofty song to the divine power among the rivers;
O Vasiṣṭha, with well-fashioned hymns and praises, magnify Sarasvatī and the two worlds.
O radiant one, since by your greatness both draughts of Soma dwell within you and the Pūrus abide [there],
be our protectress, O friend of the Maruts, and impel the bounty of the liberal patrons.
May the auspicious Sarasvatī bring us what is truly auspicious; she who is free from meanness, rich in booty, and mindful, takes heed when praised like Jamadagni and lauded like Vasiṣṭha.
Desiring wives, indeed, like those without wives, and desiring sons, O bounteous ones, we invoke Sarasvant.
O Sarasvatī, those waves of yours which are honeyed and dripping with clarity—
by means of them, be our protector.
May we enjoy the swelling breast of Sarasvatī, which is visible to all;
may we enjoy offspring and nourishment.
At the sacrifice of heaven, at the assembly of men upon earth, where the god-seeking heroes rejoice;
where for Indra the libations are pressed, may he come for exhilaration and to the first stage of life.
We choose for ourselves the divine aids; may Bṛhaspati, our friend, grant us greatness, O companions, so that we may be sinless before the Bounteous One, who is our giver from afar like a father.
Him, the eldest, the most gracious Brahmaṇaspati, I praise with homage and oblations;
may the great divine hymn attend Indra, who is the king of the prayer fashioned by the gods.
May that Bṛhaspati, the most beloved who possesses all boons, sit upon our sacred place;
may he grant us the desire for wealth and heroic strength, and carry us across our adversaries unharmed.
These immortals born of old have offered this hymn to us, acceptable to the Immortal One—Bṛhaspati, who utters a pure cry, the worshipful lord of the dwellings, the unassailable; him we invoke.
The powerful, ruddy horses, drawing him together, carry Bṛhaspati;
they clothe themselves in his ruddy form, which, though dwelling in the dark, possesses a dwelling place as brilliant as the sky.
For he is pure, the hundred-winged; he is radiant, wielding a golden axe, impetuous, and winner of light.
Bṛhaspati, sublime and easy of access, is most skilled at providing abundant nourishment for his friends.
The two divine worlds, the mothers of the god, have strengthened Bṛhaspati with their greatness.
O friends, may he, who is worthy of skill, provide for the prayer easy crossings and good paths through his power.
This well-fashioned hymn, O Brahmaṇaspati, has been made for you both—a prayer for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt.
Favor our thoughts; awaken our inspirations; exhaust the hostilities of the enemy and of those who would attack us.
O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two are the masters of celestial and terrestrial wealth. Bestow riches upon the one who praises you, even upon the humble singer. Protect us always with your blessings.
O Adhvaryus, offer the ruddy pressed stalk to the bull of the peoples!
Indra goes every day seeking the pressed Soma, desiring the drinking-place that is more familiar than even a cow.
Whatever lovely food you have desired from of old, you crave its drinking day after day;
enjoying it with both heart and mind, O Indra, drink the offered Soma juices, longing for them.
As soon as you were born, you drank Soma for the sake of power; your mother proclaimed your greatness.
O Indra, you have filled the wide mid-air; through battle, you have created space for the gods.

When we fight those who consider themselves great, may we overcome them with our arms as they display their prowess; or when, surrounded by men, O Indra, you shall fight against us, may we win that glorious battle through you.
I shall proclaim the first deeds of Indra, and those recent ones which the Bounteous Lord has performed.
When he overcame the godless illusions, then Soma became his own alone.
This entire world of cattle all around belongs to you, whatever you behold with the eye of Sūrya.
You are the sole lord of the cattle, O Indra; may we enjoy the wealth that you have bestowed.

O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two are the masters of celestial and earthly wealth. Bestow riches upon the one who praises you, even upon the humble singer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Increasing beyond all measure through your body, they do not reach the limit of your greatness.
We know both your realms upon the earth, O Viṣṇu; you, O God, alone know the highest.
O God Viṣṇu, neither one being born nor one already born has reached the furthest limit of your greatness.
You propped up the lofty, vast sky and established the eastern peak of the earth.
For you two have become possessed of refreshing food, rich in cows, and providing excellent pasture for the sake of man’s service.
O Viṣṇu, you have propped apart these two worlds; you have supported the earth on all sides with your rays.
You two have made wide space for the sacrifice, bringing forth the sun, the dawn, and the fire;
O heroes, you struck down even the magical powers of the Dāsa Vṛṣaśipra in the contests for booty.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, you shattered the ninety-nine strong fortresses of Śambara;
together you struck down a hundred and a thousand of the Asura Varcin’s heroes without resistance.

This great hymn of praise, exalting you two—the Great Ones, the Wide-Striding, the Mighty—has been offered to you both in the assemblies, O Viṣṇu; may you two swell the sacrificial foods for us in our settlements, O Indra.
O Viṣṇu, I utter the *vaṣaṭ* for you from my mouth; O Śipiviṣṭa, may you graciously accept this my oblation.
May my songs of excellent praise increase your strength. And do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Now the mortal who, desiring to gain, offers gifts to Viṣṇu, the wide-striding;
he who worships with a mind directed toward all, shall win over such a heroic one as this.
O Viṣṇu, you who travel on your own path, grant us your benevolence that extends to all people, your unfailing wisdom;
so that you may provide for us abundant prosperity, consisting of many-glittering wealth accompanied by horses.

Three times this god strode across this earth, which possesses a hundred hymns, by means of his greatness. May Viṣṇu be preeminent, more powerful than the powerful, for the name of this steadfast one is resplendent.
Viṣṇu strode across this earth for the sake of a field, bestowing it upon man;
steadfast are his praisers among men, and he of noble birth has created a wide dwelling.
Today, O Śipiviṣṭa, I, an Ārya who knows the sacred ways, proclaim that name of yours.
As one who is not yet powerful, I praise you, the powerful one, who dwells in the far distance beyond this world.
What was that which was to be hidden from you, O Viṣṇu, when you proclaimed, "I am Śipiviṣṭa"? Do not conceal this form from us, since you appeared in another form at the encounter.
O Viṣṇu, I utter the *vaṣaṭ* for you; O Śipiviṣṭa, graciously accept this my oblation.
May my songs of excellent praise increase your strength. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
Utter forth the three voices that have light as their summit, which milk this udder that yields honey. Making himself the calf, the embryo of the plants, the bull, as soon as born, bellows loudly.
He who is the increaser of the plants, he who is the lord of the waters, the god who rules over the entire moving world—
may he grant us a triple-layered refuge and protection, a threefold light for our well-being.
At one time you are barren, at another you give birth; according to his will, he has fashioned this body.
The mother receives the milk from the father; by it the father prospers, and by it the son.
In whom all beings abide, in whom the three heavens and the waters have flowed in three ways—
three vessels for pouring, overflowing with sweetness, drip honey on every side toward the mighty one.
May this speech be close to Parjanya, the self-ruling lord; may he take pleasure in it from within his heart.
May there be rain-gifts bringing us joy, and may the plants, protected by the gods, bear fine fruit for us.
He is the bull, the placer of seed for all eternal things; in him is the self of everything that moves and stands.
May that Truth protect me for a hundred autumns; and may you always protect us with blessings.
Sing forth to Parjanya, the bounteous son of Heaven;
may he seek out pasture for us.
Parjanya is he who provides the embryo for the plants, for the cows, for the horses, and for women.
Into his mouth, therefore, offer this most honey-sweet oblation; may he grant us continuous nourishment.
Having lain dormant for a year, these Brahmins who observe their vows—
the frogs— have uttered forth their voices, which have been quickened by Parjanya.
When the divine waters flowed over him as he lay like a dried-up skin in the pool,
then the croaking of the frogs comes together here like the lowing of cows that have calves.
When rain has fallen upon these longing, thirsty ones at the arrival of the monsoon,
one goes toward the other who speaks, as a son, having mocked his father.
One seizes the other as these two rejoice when the waters are released;
when the frog, rained upon, croaks aloud, the speckled one joins his voice with the green one.
When one of them repeats the speech of another, like a pupil learning from a master,
all that of theirs is as if perfectly joined, even as you of eloquent voice speak upon the waters.
One has the cry of a jackal, one the cry of a goat; one of them is speckled, one is green. Bearing a common name, though diverse in form, they have fashioned their voices in many ways as they speak.
Like Brahmins at the Atirātra Soma sacrifice, speaking around a full pool as if in concert,
you frogs occupy that day of the year which has become the rainy season.
The Soma-offering Brahmins have raised their voice, performing the sacred prayer that lasts throughout the year;
the Adhvaryu priests, sweating over the heated milk-vessels, appear openly, none of them remaining hidden.
They have guarded the divine ordinance of the twelfth month; these men do not neglect the season. When the rainy season has arrived at the end of the year, the heated libations attain their release.

The bull-like one has given, the goat-like one has given; the speckled one and the yellow one have given us riches. The frogs, giving hundreds of cattle, prolong our lives at the thousandfold pressing.
O Indra and Soma, burn up the Rakṣas; crush them down, O Bulls, and cast those who thrive in darkness into the depths.
Shatter the senseless ones, consume them with fire, slay them, drive them away, and strike down the devouring Atriṇs.
O Indra and Soma, let the evil against the one who intends evil boil up like a cauldron filled with fire.
Against the hater of sacred prayer, the eater of raw flesh, the one of terrible gaze, and the *kimīdin*, bestow relentless hatred.

O Indra and Soma, pierce the evildoers within the cave, into the darkness where there is no support, so that not even one of them may rise up from there again; let that be your wrathful and conquering power.
O Indra and Soma, hurl down from heaven and from earth your weapon, the crusher of the one who speaks evil. Fashion from the mountains your celestial bolt with which you burn up the waxing *rakṣas*.
O Indra and Soma, turn them back from heaven with your stone-hurling bolts heated by fire;
with your unaging, heat-armed weapons, pierce the Atriṇas into the abyss so that they go forth voiceless.
O Indra and Soma, may this prayer encompass you on every side, as a girth-girth encircles two prize-winning horses.
This oblation which I present to you with wisdom—quicken these sacred formulations (*brahmāṇi*), O lords of men, as if quickening two kings.
May you two take heed with your impetuous courses, striking down the malicious and treacherous demons.
O Indra and Soma, let there be no easy path for the evildoer who at any time assails us with malice.
He who, with a simple mind, accuses me—who walk upright—with false words, may that speaker, O Indra, be held fast like water in the hollow of the hand; may he sink down into the depths.
Those who, by their ways, scatter the one who speaks simply, or those who with their own powers corrupt what is auspicious—
may Soma deliver them over to the serpent, or place them in the lap of Destruction.

O Agni, whoever seeks to harm our essence of food, or those of our horses, or those of our cattle, or those of our own bodies—let that enemy, thief, and doer of theft go to destruction; let him be utterly deprived of both his body and his progeny.
May he be far away from us in body and in progeny; may he lie beneath all the three earths.
May his glory wither away, O gods, who seeks to harm us by day and who seeks to harm us by night.

To the discerning person, truth and falsehood are easily distinguished; these two words contend with one another. Of these two, that which is true and more upright—Soma protects that very thing and slays the untrue.
Indeed, Soma does not favor the crooked man, nor the warrior who maintains his position through deceit.
He slays the Rakṣas and slays the one who speaks falsely; both lie ensnared in the noose of Indra.
If I have been one whose gods are falsehood, or if I have held the gods in vain, O Agni—why, O Jātavedas, art thou angry with us? May those of deceitful speech fall into destruction!
May I die this very day if I am a sorcerer, or if I have consumed the vital breath of a man;
then may he be deprived of his ten sons who falsely calls me a sorcerer.
May Indra slay with his great weapon him who says of me, "I am a sorcerer," or the demon who says, "I am pure"; may he fall as the lowest of all living beings.
She who comes forth at night like an owl, hiding her body with malice—may she fall into the endless pits;
may the pressing-stones strike down the demons with their clanging sounds.

Spread out, O Maruts, search among the people; seize them and crush the Rākṣasas—those who fly about at night having become birds, or those who have placed their hostility toward the divine sacrifice.
O Indra, Maghavan, hurl down the stone from heaven; sharpened by Soma, whet it well. From the east, from the west, from below, and from above, strike down the demons with the mountain.
These very ones fly about like dog-wolves; seeking to harm, they wish to injure Indra, the unassailable.
Śakra whets his weapon for the treacherous; he shall now surely hurl his thunderbolt at the sorcerers.
Indra became the destroyer of the sorcerers who plunder the oblation as they seek to attack;
indeed, the powerful one goes toward the Rākṣasas, shattering them like an axe through a forest or like a vessel being broken.
Slay the owl-demon, slay the screech-owl demon; slay the dog-demon and the cuckoo-demon. Slay the eagle-demon and the vulture-demon; O Indra, crush the *rakṣas* like a millstone.
May the demon of those possessing sorcery not overwhelm us; may he drive away the paired *kimīdins*.
May the Earth protect us from earthly distress, and may the mid-air protect us from celestial distress.
O Indra, slay the male sorcerer and the female who exults in her magic power. Let the fools who worship false gods perish with broken necks; let them not see the sun as it rises.
Look out, look around; O Indra and Soma, be watchful! Cast forth your weapon at the Rākṣasas, hurl your thunderbolt at the sorcerers.
